articles.title: El Valencia aprieta el 'botón rojo'
articles.standfirst: Casino Gran Madrid todavía no sitúa al conjunto 'che' como uno de los tres principales candidatos al descenso
articles.summary: Casino Gran Madrid todavía no sitúa al conjunto 'che' como uno de los tres principales candidatos al descenso
articles.body: Sólo se han disputado cinco jornadas de LaLiga, pero el Valencia ya ha tomado una decisión drástica que evidencia la preocupación que existe en Mestalla. El conjunto 'che' ha destituido a Carlos Corberán, apenas unos meses después de haber renovado su contrato, tras un inicio de temporada mucho más preocupante de lo esperado. El mercado de fichajes ya había dejado algunas dudas sobre las posibilidades del equipo en el que será el último curso en Mestalla. Pero los primeros resultados han terminado por encender todas las alarmas. El Valencia comenzó el campeonato con un empate ante el Celta y, desde entonces, sólo ha conocido la derrota. Betis, Deportivo, Barcelona y Sevilla han encadenado cuatro triunfos consecutivos que han llevado al conjunto valencianista hasta el último puesto de la clasificación. Un escenario que ha terminado provocando el primer cambio de entrenador de la temporada en LaLiga. Las apuestas deportivas también han reaccionado al mal arranque, aunque todavía existe cierta confianza en que el Valencia pueda revertir la situación antes de que la amenaza del descenso sea realmente preocupante. De hecho, Casino Gran Madrid todavía no coloca al conjunto 'che' entre los tres principales candidatos a perder la categoría. Su cuota para el descenso es actualmente de 3.15, por detrás de Málaga (1.80), Elche (2.05) y Racing (2.90), y ligeramente por encima del Levante (3.10). La destitución de Corberán, eso sí, supone un nuevo capítulo en la complicada etapa del club bajo la propiedad de Peter Lim tras convertirse en el decimotercer entrenador destituido por el Valencia en los últimos 12 años. Una cifra que refleja la inestabilidad de un proyecto que vuelve a encontrarse ante una situación límite. Ahora, el club deberá encontrar rápidamente un nuevo responsable para el banquillo. Braulio ya ha asumido el cargo de director deportivo y trabaja en la búsqueda de un candidato que pueda cambiar el rumbo del equipo. Ahora bien, el calendario no ofrece margen para reaccionar. El Valencia tendrá que afrontar entre semana su próximo compromiso ante un Alavés que, pese a su reciente derrota contra el Racing, está protagonizando un inicio de temporada notable. Las mejores casas de apuestas tampoco esperan un partido sencillo para los valencianistas. Casino Gran Madrid sitúa al Alavés como favorito para llevarse los tres puntos, con una cuota de 1.83, mientras que el empate se paga a 3.25 y la victoria del Valencia alcanza los 5.0. El cambio de entrenador llega, por tanto, en uno de los peores momentos posibles, con un equipo necesitado de reaccionar y un rival directo que ha comenzado con mejores sensaciones. El Valencia ha apretado el 'botón rojo' demasiado pronto... y ahora necesita que la decisión tenga un efecto inmediato.

articles.title: Chargers' defense struggles in first outing under new coordinator Chris O'Leary
articles.summary: Mike McDaniel wasn’t the only Los Angeles Chargers coordinator to have a bad debut on Sunday.  Chris O’Leary’s defense got off to a rough start in a 26-14 lo...
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. (AP) — Mike McDaniel wasn't the only Los Angeles Chargers coordinator to have a bad debut on Sunday .

Chris O'Leary's defense got off to a rough start in a 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals , struggling in nearly every area.

A drop-off was expected after Jesse Minter left to become coach of the Baltimore Ravens , but O'Leary's hiring was supposed to minimize it. He had familiarity with the Chargers, having coached safeties in 2024 before spending one season at Western Michigan as defensive coordinator. O'Leary would keep the system in place, putting his own stamp on a 4-2-5 defense using three safeties, to allow an experienced roster to keep playing fast and aggressive.

Instead, they were consistently on their heels against first-time head coach Mike LaFleur, who also called offensive plays.

The Chargers couldn't get their opposition off schedule, allowing five straight drives that ended in a touchdown or field goal attempt before finally forcing a punt late in the third quarter.

An accomplished pass rush rarely laid a hand on journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett , with linebackers Daiyan Henley and Troy Dye combining for the only sack on a rare blitz. That inability to control the line of scrimmage extended to the run defense, managing one tackle for loss on 34 carries. Failing to generate a takeaway completed the trilogy of passiveness.

Those issues had a carryover effect on the offense, forcing McDaniel to get away from his trademark ground game while playing from behind.

Coach Jim Harbaugh likely approached the season thinking McDaniel's potent offense would help offset the loss of one of the best defensive minds in football, giving O'Leary time to learn on the job. Instead, neither coordinator could help out the other in the opener.

The defense buckled down in the red zone, forcing Arizona to settle for three field goals in five visits to keep the game from getting completely out of hand.

Where to begin? Among the many glaring issues coming out of the opener, the offense's inability to sustain drives was particularly galling. The Chargers were 2 of 8 on third down and 0 for 3 on fourth down. Their only successful conversion in the second half was Justin Herbert 's touchdown pass to get within 16-14 midway through the third quarter.

After taking a step back last season, WR Ladd McConkey got off to a good start with five receptions for 82 yards and a touchdown. He could have been even more productive had a chest injury not forced him out of the game in the third quarter.

WR Quentin Johnston caught just two of his seven targets for 17 yards, starting his fourth season in Los Angeles . It has been an often frustrating tenure since he was drafted in the first round in 2023.

McConkey underwent further testing on his ribs and is day to day. ... CB Elijah Molden hurt his hamstring. ... WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith is likely to miss several weeks because of a pulled hamstring.

68.6% — Herbert dropped back to pass or ran the ball on 35 of the Chargers' 51 offense snaps, with McDaniel's first game looking a little too much like previous campaigns where the star quarterback was asked to do everything.

The Chargers host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. With back-to-back road games at Buffalo and Seattle on deck as part of a tough seven-game stretch, failure to win against their AFC West rivals could quickly leave Los Angeles' playoff hopes in dire straits.

articles.title: Bills open season in familiar fashion with Josh Allen still patching over defensive deficiencies
articles.summary: As first impressions go, the new-look Buffalo Bills under Joe Brady opened the season looking much like the team previously coached by Sean McDermott.  Josh...
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — As first impressions go, the new-look Buffalo Bills under Joe Brady opened the season looking much like the team previously coached by Sean McDermott.

And that's not an altogether good thing.

Josh Allen was a near one-man offensive show in a 36-31 win at Houston that featured eight lead changes, including four in the final quarter. He threw two TD passes and had two rushing for his 25th four-touchdown career outing; improved to 24-8 when topping 300 yards passing; and pulled out the victory with his 26th game-winning drive.

Breathtaking as the performance was, it was also reminiscent of the recent past with Allen once again required to patch over the defense's deficiencies . This was one of the reasons the Bills changed course in January by firing McDermott after Buffalo's defensive dud in a 33-30 overtime playoff loss to Denver .

Though on Sunday the defense came up with a victory-sealing stop on Greg Rousseau 's strip-sack of C.J. Stroud with 9 seconds remaining at the Bills 18, it marked one of the few times Buffalo got the Texans off the field.

The Bills allowed 124 yards rushing, a year after allowing 120 or more eight times in a game.

The Bills allowed Houston to convert 7 of 16 third down opportunities, including four of 8 yards or longer, and both fourth down attempts.

The Texans scored on four of five drives inside the Buffalo 20.

The 26 first downs surrendered by Buffalo were the most in a game since December 2024.

If it's any consolation, first-year coordinator Jim Leonhard acknowledged there's much room for improvement.

"I love the way we started by creating a turnover and then finishing it out with a big turnover. There was a lot of ugly in between," he said on Monday. "It did feel like Week 1, when things started to unravel a little bit at times or feel a little bit off, I thought our guys looked around like they weren't sure what the answer should be."

The defense was expected to go through an early season break-in period given Buffalo introduced four new starters while making the switch to a three-lineman/four linebacker system.

Leonhard said he's still learning his unit's strengths, while also expressing confidence the defense is still tracking on an upward trajectory.

"We're closer than it looked. And I'm excited for where we're going," he said.

The test doesn't get any easier with Buffalo facing a short week and preparing to host the high-octane Detroit Lions on Thursday night.

The previous time the teams met in December 2024, Allen threw for two TDs and ran for two more in a 48-42 win in an outing the Lions scored touchdowns on each of their final four possessions.

Big-play offense. Buffalo scored 36 points on just 52 offensive snaps. The Bills combined for 10 plays on two touchdown drives each starting at their 4.

Defensive stops. The Texans had 73 offensive snaps (the most by a Bills opponent since they beat Detroit), and finished with a near 13-minute edge in time of possession.

WR DJ Moore . The offseason veteran trade acquisition built on the chemistry he developed with Allen this summer. Moore finished with five catches for 100 yards and drew a 46-yard pass interference penalty in the end zone to set up Allen's 1-yard touchdown run.

RB Ray Davis . The primary backup to James Cook was limited to playing five offensive snaps, while practice squad call-up Frank Gore Jr. played 11 and most notably in pass-blocking situations.

LB Terrel Bernard was listed as having a calf injury, and deemed a limited participant in practice Monday. S Cole Bishop (knee/groin) and edge rusher Bradley Chubb (thumb) were listed as full practice participants.

130 — Dalton Kincaid 's yards receiving, the third most by a Bills tight end in team history. Paul Costa had 163- and 138-yard outings in 1967.

Face a short turnaround and whatever additional nerves that could come with a desire of having to put on a show to open their new stadium hosting the Lions.

articles.title: Rafael Nadal bought 7,000-sq-metre Mallorca clifftop plot for €4 million after €5.7 million asking price, then spent 3 years rebuilding it as his family home
articles.summary: International Sports News: Rafael Nadal spent €4 million on a 7,000-square-metre coastal property in Porto Cristo, Mallorca, after it was originally listed for €5.7 million. The.
articles.body: Rafael Nadal spent €4 million on a 7,000-square-metre coastal property in Porto Cristo, Mallorca, after it was originally listed for €5.7 million. The 22-time Grand Slam champion bought the land and an old Majorcan stone house in 2013, then later replaced the original buildings with a modern family home. The property sits above Porto Cristo’s harbour and has wide views of the Mediterranean. Construction on the new home began after Nadal married Maria Francisca Perelló in 2019 and was completed in 2023. Today, the estate remains closely tied to Nadal’s life in Mallorca.How did Rafael Nadal buy the Porto Cristo property for €4 millionThe property Rafael Nadal bought in 2013 was not a new luxury villa. It included a traditional Majorcan stone chalet and other buildings spread across about 7,000 square metres of land on the coast of Porto Cristo. The estate had belonged to the heirs of people linked to the development of the nearby Caves of Drach, one of Mallorca’s best-known attractions.The asking price was €5.7 million, but Nadal eventually agreed to pay €4 million. That meant he secured the property for about €1.7 million less than the original asking price.The location was also important. Porto Cristo is on Mallorca’s eastern coast and is close to Manacor, where Nadal was born and where his tennis academy is based. The property gave him a private home near his family and the part of the island that has remained central to his life.The purchase was reported by the Majorca Daily Bulletin in 2020, when the property was still being rebuilt. At the time, the publication described the site as a 7,000-square-metre coastal estate with the old stone chalet still on it.What did Rafael Nadal build on the 7,000-square-metre siteNadal did not simply update the old house. The original buildings were taken down as part of a much bigger project, and a new home was designed for the family.Mallorcan architect Tomeu Esteva worked on the project. The finished property has a modern look but still fits its coastal setting. Large windows bring the sea views into the main living areas, while stone and other natural materials keep the design connected to Mallorca.The home includes large outdoor areas, terraces and an infinity pool facing the harbour. The layout also gives the family plenty of private space away from the public areas of Porto Cristo.Architectural Digest reported that the home sits on a 1.7-acre plot overlooking the port and described it as Nadal’s main home in Mallorca. The publication also noted that Esteva designed the modern villa after the original property was acquired by Nadal.The size of the land is one of the biggest features of the estate. Instead of building a home that dominates the site, the project uses the coastal position, views and outdoor space as major parts of the property.When was Rafael Nadal’s Mallorca home finally completedThe rebuild took several years. Work began after Nadal and Maria Francisca Perelló married in October 2019, but the project was not finished quickly.Building a large home on a coastal site involved a long planning and construction process. By 2023, the work was finally close to completion, and the family began using the property as their home.In September 2023, Nadal himself gave followers a glimpse of the finished property. He shared a photograph from the infinity pool, with Porto Cristo’s harbour visible behind him, and wrote, “Working,” alongside Bon Jovi’s “It’s My Life.”The Majorca Daily Bulletin reported at the time that the work had been completed at the start of that summer. It also noted that the property’s interconnected buildings sit on the 7,000-square-metre plot and that Nadal could see his catamaran, Great White, from the home.That timing also made the house especially significant in Nadal’s life. He retired from professional tennis in November 2024 after a career that included 22 Grand Slam singles titles. The Porto Cristo home was therefore already in place as he moved into life away from the regular demands of the ATP Tour.Why is Porto Cristo important to Rafael Nadal and Maria Francisca PerellóFor Nadal, the property is not simply another expensive home. Its location keeps him close to Manacor, the town where he grew up and where his family has deep roots.Nadal’s parents live nearby, while the Rafa Nadal Academy is also in Manacor. The academy opened in 2016 and has become an important part of his work away from the professional tour.The Porto Cristo property also puts Nadal close to the sea. His 80-foot Sunreef Power catamaran, Great White, was delivered in 2020. Sunreef Yachts confirmed that Nadal commissioned the boat and designed it with family use and time on the water in mind.That connection between the house and the sea has been visible in photographs Nadal has shared from the property. The home overlooks the harbour, while the yacht is kept nearby, making it easy for Nadal and his family to spend time on the water.The estate is also the family home for Nadal, Perelló and their children. Their first son, Rafael, was born in October 2022, while their second son, Miquel, was born in August 2025.What other property does Rafael Nadal own outside MallorcaThe Porto Cristo estate is not Nadal’s only major property. He has also owned a home in the Dominican Republic, where he bought a villa in the Playa Nueva Romana resort.His property holdings have also expanded to Madrid. In March 2024, the Majorca Daily Bulletin reported that Nadal had bought a luxury home in the Spanish capital. The residence was described as a 280-square-metre property with four bedrooms and five bathrooms, along with shared facilities including a spa and gym.Nadal has also moved into the hospitality business. He partnered with Meliá Hotels International to launch the ZEL hotel brand, which combines the Nadal name with a Mediterranean lifestyle theme.Still, Porto Cristo has a different role from those investments. The Madrid home serves a major city, the Dominican Republic property is a holiday retreat and the ZEL project is a business venture. The Mallorca estate is tied directly to Nadal’s family life and his connection to the island where his tennis story began.The €4 million purchase therefore became much more than a property deal. Nadal bought a large piece of the Mallorca coast at a significant discount to its original asking price, rebuilt it over several years and turned it into a private home overlooking Porto Cristo. With his professional career now over, the property gives him a permanent base close to Manacor, his family and the sea.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: WWE Raw Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights of Roman Reigns vs. Penta and Full Show
articles.summary: WWE's stint in Mexico City continued Monday on Raw with a Netflix broadcast headlined by a blockbuster main event with high stakes.
articles.body:
WWE's stint in Mexico City continued Monday on Raw with a Netflix broadcast headlined by a blockbuster main event with high stakes.

Did Roman Reigns successfully retain his World Heavyweight Championship when he defended against Penta, or did the hometown hero relieve the OTC of his gold, making it three successive shows south of the border with a new champion crowned?

Find out in this recap, including grades and analysis for the entire show.

World Heavyweight Championship Match: Penta vs. Roman Reigns (c)

Intercontinental Championship Match: Chad Gable (c) vs. Dragon Lee

Women's Money in the Bank Qualifying Match: Raquel Rodriguez vs. Kelani Jordan vs. Lola Vice

Men's Money in the Bank Qualifying Match: Je'Von Evans vs. Big Cass vs. Austin Theory

Last Time in Action: Rey Mysterio lost to Omos (AAA Triplemania, September 11)

Sporting a neck brace following a vicious attack from Omos at AAA Triplemania, the 2023 Hall of Famer kicked off the show, addressing the fans and throwing to a recap of Stephanie Vaquer's Women's World Championship victory over Liv Morgan on Saturday night in Chile.

La Primera joined Mysterio in the ring, drawing a huge ovation from the Mexico City audience, and expressed the joy of winning the title in her home country and the pride she has in representing Mexico.

Liv Morgan and Dominik Mysterio interrupted, drawing a chorus of boos from the audience, the fans nearly drowning out the latter as he reprimanded his father.

El Grande Americano, the new AAA Mega Champion after defeating Dirty Dom 24 hours earlier, arrived to a deafening pop and a Mixed Tag team Match was announced to kick off the in-ring portion of the show.

WWE could not have possibly started a show hotter than this, for this audience. The crowd ate all of it up, Vaquer showed great emotion, Mysterio was the perfect option to welcome Mexico City to Netflix, and the Mixed Tag Team Match featuring the beloved Americano was a stellar creative decision.

El Grande Americano and Stephanie Vaquer vs. Liv Morgan and Dominik Mysterio

Last Time in Action: El Grande Americano defeated Dominik Mysterio (AAA Triplemania, September 13); Liv Morgan defeated Stephanie Vaquer (Raw, September 7)

The Judgment Day, as it tends to do, arrived just in the nick of time to ruin the opening contest of Monday's show.

A high-energy, red-hot Mixed Tag Team Match pitting Americano and Vaquer against Mysterio and Morgan was progressing perfectly, with La Primera delivering a 619 to both opponents and the babyfaces setting up for the win.

The arrival of Roxanne Perez, Raquel Rodriguez, and JD McDonagh turned the numbers game in the heels' favor and ensured the segment ended with the villainous faction standing tall to close it out.

Before that, fans were treated to two mini matches within the context of a bigger one, each appropriately good with enough connective tissue to pass for one overarching bout.

All four Superstars were excellent, the crowd ate it up, and the only negative was the decision to book the non-finish just to rebuild heat for a faction that typically does not have problems with that.

Americano and Vaquer defeated Morgan and Mysterio via disqualification

Vaquer and Americano have so much in-ring personality. They were excellent here, feeding off the audience and playing to it when the time called for it.

Would it have hurt for the babyfaces to have one more triumphant night in Mexico City?

Money in the Bank Qualifier: Je'Von Evans vs. Austin Theory vs. Big Cass

Last Time in Action: Je'Von Evans defeated Dominik Mysterio via disqualification (Raw, August 28); Big Cass defeated Brooks Jensen (Main Event, September 10); Austin Theory lost to Otis (Raw, September 7)

Maxxine Dupri attempted to run interference for her boyfriend Theory, distracting Cass at ringside. It did not work. Instead, Evans drove him into the giant, then proceeded to outmaneuver Cass, deliver the OG Cutter, and score the victory.

A good, energetic match that built nicely and only got a little messy late, it featured a pleasant surprise outcome, with Evans cashing his ticket to Money in the Bank, where he joins Bron Breakker in the namesake ladder match.

Theory held this one together nicely. For all of the issues that some have with his character, he is a spectacularly solid wrestler who probably does not get the credit he has earned for his in-ring work.

Interesting to see Big Cass eat the fall here when the aforementioned Theory was right there . Considering the lengths to which WWE has gone to rejuvenate The Vision after last week's Sunday Night's Main Event and Raw, it makes sense that the creative team would not want to beat Theory. Why book itself into a corner by beating Cass, though?

Intercontinental Championship Match: Dragon Lee vs. Chad Gable

Last Time in Action: Dragon Lee, Penta, and Rey Fenix defeated Los Perros del Mal (AAA Ola del Calor) ; Chad Gable defeated Rey Mysterio (Raw, August 17)

Two of the best wrestlers on the Raw brand wowed the fans in Mexico City with a competitive battle for the Intercontinental Championship as Gable defended against Lee.

The challenger threw himself around the squared circle early and often, wiping the champion out and putting him on the defensive entering the break.

Back from the timeout, champion and challenger traded blows, each looking for the knockout that would earn them the title. Gable targeted the ankle, looking for his trademark submission, but Lee answered with a double stomp to the floor.

Later, he survived a moonsault from Gable to deliver Operation Dragon, but could only hold the champion down for two. Chants of "esto es lucha!" rained from the stands as Lee countered out of an ankle lock, delivered the Styles Clash, but still could not keep Gable down for three.

Gable grabbed the ankle and forced the tapout moments later, but took time to express respect for Lee, to the appreciation of the Mexico City fans.

Not that it should surprise anyone, but this was a hellish match. Gable and Lee tore the house down in a great one, featuring plenty of drama, a red-hot crowd, and some jaw-dropping athletic feats.

The right person went over as so much time and energy, two year's worth to be exact, went into Gable winning the gold.

With that said, Lee has had copious bangers over the last year and really should be rewarded with a consistent push instead of being relied on to be "the other guy" in great matches.

Women's Money in the Bank Qualifier: Lola Vice vs. Kelani Jordan vs. Raquel Rodriguez

Last Time in Action: Lola Vice lost to Kendal Grey (NXT, August 4); Kelani Jordan defeated Jaida Parker (NXT, September 8); Raquel Rodriguez defeated Sol Ruca (Raw, August 28)

Vice capped off her main roster debut with a rollup on Rodriguez that earned her the win over Big Sexy and NXT Women's Champion Jordan and a spot in the Money in the Bank match.

A competitive bout that saw Vice waste little time acclimating herself on the Raw brand by taking the fight to her opponents from the opening bell, it appropriately spotlighted all three competitors.

The NXT exports highlighted what about them made them breakout stars in the first place, while Rodriguez kept them at bay, looking to cash her ticket to New Orleans.

Unfortunately for the Judgment Day muscle, Vice scored the win with a rollup and appears fast-tracked toward success on the flagship.

In a match with a lightning-quick pace at times, neither Jordan nor Vice looked out of place as they competed for a spot in Money in the Bank. Their work was crisp, their timing was mostly perfect, and they highlighted themselves well to an audience that may not be as familiar with their work as others.

Rodriguez was great here. She was the experienced veteran tasked with holding the match together. It helped that Vice and Jordan have a rich history with each other, but working on TV, on Monday Night Raw, is a completely different beast. She made sure everything went well and even finds herself with a potentially new challenger in Vice.

Jordan is ready to be called up now, but the lack of spots on Raw or SmackDown means she is better off being the standard-bearer for the brand she was introduced and evolved on.

World Heavyweight Championship Match: Penta vs. Roman Reigns

Last Time in Action: Penta, Rey Fenix, and Dragon Lee defeated Los Perros del Mal (AAA Ola del Calor, August 30); Roman Reigns defeated Seth Rollins (SummerSlam, August 2)

The atmosphere was otherworldly as Penta and Reigns came face to face during the introductions for Monday's main event.

Penta controlled early while Reigns seized control entering the commercial break. The challenger shook it off and put The OTC on the defensive. Grabbing hold of the champion's arm, Penta delivered the Sacrifice, snapping the limb straight back and sending Reigns scurrying in pain.

The Tribal Chief dropped Penta on the ring apron, then followed with a powerbomb on the announce table. It did not take the fight out of the challenger, who delivered a Penta Driver for a dramatic near-fall that reignited the crowd.

High drama reigned supreme late in the bout as Penta delivered a Mexican Destroyer, only to eat a spear from Reigns. The Tribal Chief was left in disbelief as Penta shot his shoulder off the mat to avoid the three-count.

Frustrated, he talked trash to Penta, then grabbed the microphone to demand acknowledgement from the Mexico City fans. The challenger did just that, in the form of another Mexican Destroyer, but Reigns kicked out.

An exchange of blows gave way to a springboard attempt by Penta, who landed face-first in a Superman Punch. A spear later and Reigns successfully retained the gold.

This is the best Reigns we have ever seen. Perhaps he is on a revenge tour, hellbent to remind the audience of who the top guy in WWE really is, but he is on a streak of main event matches that have each been Match of the Year contenders.

Get Penta in the main event scene now. Put him there, keep him there. This was his biggest test and he passed it with flying colors. He was fantastic, as he has been consistently, and has earned that jump to the next level.

The chemistry here was off the charts, too. Who would have thought we would see Reigns sell two Mexican Destroyers, let alone one?

It is a testament to the show as a whole that determining the MVP of this broadcast was as difficult as it is. With that said, the weight of the world was on Penta to prove he could hang with Reigns in the main event, in front of a rabid audience ready to see him win the World Heavyweight Championship.

The luchador did just that, proving himself worthy of sharing the ring with one of the measuring sticks in WWE and, even in defeat, coming out of it looking like a genuine main event star.

In his first real test of his main event value, he passed with flying colors and earned another look in the title picture sooner rather than later.

Recency bias be damned, this was one of the greatest episodes of WWE Raw of all time. An elite crowd, a card that featured nothing bad or even mid, for that matter, and a main event that would have been right at home on a premium live event card, this was a sign of what WWE is capable of when motivated to produce the best possible product.

We saw some NXT stars shine, a tremendously fun opening Mixed Tag Team Match, two quality Money in the Bank qualifiers, and a breakout performance from a luchador who should already be a fixture in the main event.

articles.title: Welles Crowther’s inspiring 9/11 story: How a former Boston College lacrosse player became the man in the red bandana
articles.summary: International Sports News: Twenty-five years after September 11, 2001, the story of Welles Crowther still carries a powerful message about courage. A former Boston College lacro.
articles.body: Twenty-five years after September 11, 2001, the story of Welles Crowther still carries a powerful message about courage. A former Boston College lacrosse player working in the World Trade Center, Crowther chose to help others when thousands were trying to escape. His red bandana became a symbol of hope for survivors and a lasting reminder of one man’s extraordinary decision to put strangers before himself.Welles Crowther and the red bandana that became his legacyCrowther had carried a red bandana since childhood. His father gave it to him when he was six, and it eventually became part of his identity.Long before the tragedy, Crowther had already shown an interest in helping others. At 16, he signed up to become a junior firefighter. His father, Jefferson Crowther, later remembered a conversation that showed where his son's ambitions were heading.“Welles called me one day and said, ‘I think I want to change my career,’ ” his father, Jefferson Crowther, recalled in a 2019 ESPN feature, The Man in the Red Bandana. “He said, ‘I think I want to be a New York City firefighter.’ ”Instead, Crowther began a career in finance. In 1999, he joined an equity firm and worked on the 104th floor of the South Tower.On September 11, 2001, his professional life became secondary to something far more urgent.After the attacks, survivors recalled a young man moving through the smoke and confusion, helping injured people and directing them toward safety. They did not know his name. They remembered the red bandana covering his face.One survivor, Ling Young, later described the moment Crowther appeared.“A young man come out of nowhere. This man’s voice said, ‘I found the stairs, follow me and only help the ones you can help.’ It was the way he said it, we just got up and we followed.”Crowther helped people reach a functioning stairwell and guided them toward firefighters. But rather than leaving with those he had helped, he went back upstairs.That decision became the defining part of his story.The man in the red bandana became a 9/11 heroCrowther continued moving through the South Tower, helping people escape and providing assistance to those who were injured. Judy Wein was among those he helped, according to accounts later shared by her husband, Gerry.“She had just come out of surgery,” Gerry recalled of the days after the terrorist attack. “At that point, she could hardly speak but she wanted to tell me what happened. She said a young man appeared out of nowhere. She watched as he went around helping people, putting out fires and administering aid to the injured,” he recalled.For Crowther’s parents, the mystery surrounding their son’s final hours lasted for months. They eventually learned about the unidentified rescuer described by survivors. When they showed photographs of Crowther, survivors recognized him as the man who had guided them.Crowther’s body was later found in the lobby of the South Tower alongside firefighters. Accounts credit him with helping as many as 12 people survive the attacks.His actions also created a legacy that reached far beyond New York.In 2006, Crowther was posthumously named a New York City firefighter. That same year, his Boston College teammate Tyler Jewell honored him while competing in the Winter Olympics.“For me, the red bandana symbolizes everything I want to be and everything Welles was,” Jewell said in The Man in the Red Bandana. “Strength, honor, courage — he’s a true hero.”The red bandana has since become closely associated with Crowther’s memory at Boston College. The school’s annual Red Bandanna Game keeps his story alive for a new generation of students and athletes.The tradition is more than a tribute to a former lacrosse player. It reflects the values that Crowther displayed when his own safety was at stake.His story remains striking because he did not know the people he helped. He had no guarantee that anyone would remember his name. He simply saw people who needed help and acted.That is why Welles Crowther’s legacy has endured. The red bandana is easy to remember, but the choice behind it is what made him a hero.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Did Lewis Hamilton plan to marry Kim Kardashian for custody reasons? Viral ‘father figure’ claim debunked
articles.summary: International Sports News: A social media post claiming Lewis Hamilton plans to marry Kim Kardashian to help her in a custody fight with Kanye West is not backed by any credible.
articles.body: A social media post claiming Lewis Hamilton plans to marry Kim Kardashian to help her in a custody fight with Kanye West is not backed by any credible evidence. It also says Hamilton wants to become a father figure to North West because of alleged behavior problems. There is no verified statement from Hamilton supporting those claims. The post uses an Esquire interview clip and a separate photo of Hamilton with Kardashian and a young girl, but those images do not prove the story. There are no credible report carrying the alleged comments.Lewis Hamilton and Kim Kardashian have publicly grown closerHamilton and Kardashian’s relationship has become more public in 2026, but that does not support the custody claim. Elle reported in August that the pair had known each other since at least 2014 and first went public together at the 2026 Super Bowl. Their relationship later became more open.Hamilton also spoke about Kardashian after the Monaco Grand Prix in June, where she watched him finish second for Ferrari. He said, “It is amazing to have her come this weekend and to have that support.“It is amazing to have good people around you, good people supporting you, and she does that for me every day.”He later acknowledged Kardashian again at the British Grand Prix. P reported that when Hamilton was asked about his happiness and support, he said, “And of course, of course, it’s Kim.”The couple has also been seen spending time with Kardashian’s children. Those family moments show that he has become part of their social life, but they do not show that he is taking any legal role involving the children.Kim Kardashian, Kanye West and the custody claimKardashian and West share four children, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. Their divorce was finalized in 2022, and they agreed to joint custody. That arrangement is important because the viral post presents Hamilton’s alleged marriage plan as if it would directly change the custody situation. There is no evidence that he has made such a proposal or that a marriage to Kardashian would automatically give him a role in the custody case.The claim about North West’s alleged behavioral issues is also unsupported.The same problem applies to the new Hamilton claim. The Esquire clip and the photo attached to the post are not evidence of the words attributed to him. No credible interview, statement or report has surfaced confirming that Hamilton wants to marry Kardashian for custody reasons or become North’s father figure.Hamilton and Kardashian may face continued speculation about marriage as their relationship develops, but as of September 2026, there is no confirmed engagement or wedding announcement from either of them. The custody-focused claim should therefore be treated as unverified, not as a statement of Hamilton’s plans.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: 'The mistakes I made, I won't make again' - Sprinter Animesh Kujur ready for a bigger challenge
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: By the time Animesh Kujur lined up for the 200m at the Indian Athletics Series Final at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi last week, the instructi.
articles.body: By the time Animesh Kujur lined up for the 200m at the Indian Athletics Series Final at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi last week, the instruction from his coach was fairly simple: don't chase the clock.It was getting late. The priority was to stay injury-free, execute the bend and finish the race.Kujur won in 20.59 seconds after winning the 100m in 10.21 seconds. Gurindervir Singh, India's 100m national record holder, was second in 10.32.The meeting was the final domestic stop before the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. For Kujur, the two victories were less about producing another headline time than getting through the evening and into the final phase of his preparation.“The coach said that the time is getting late, so just stay injury-free. Don't push too much. Just try to come first,” Kujur told TimesofIndia.com after the race. “Just try to execute the curve. That's it. And I just did it like that. I came straight and just maintained my pace. And just finished the race.”He arrives in Aichi-Nagoya with a 10.14 personal best in the 100m and the national 200m record of 20.32, set at the 2025 Asian Championships. He will compete in the 100m, 200m and relay.The 10.14 came in Wetzlar, Germany, in July and remains the second-fastest 100m by an Indian, behind Gurindervir's 10.09 national record. Kujur's run was also the fastest 100m by an Indian outside the country.Gurindervir's 10.09 came at the Federation Cup in Ranchi in May, when the Indian record changed hands repeatedly over a short period. Kujur had run 10.15 before Gurindervir reclaimed the record with 10.09.The two have continued to race each other through the season. At the Series Final in Delhi, Kujur had the better of the two again.Kujur said that competition has changed the way he feels about the 100m.“I will say 100, I am having more fun now because I am getting competition from Guri again and again,” he said.He does not feel the same level of competition in the 200m.“In 200, there is not as much competition as there should be in India,” he said. “But when you get competition, that is when you enjoy running fast.”The Asian Games will give him plenty of it.A tougher sprint field awaits in Aichi-NagoyaJapan's Shuhei Tada and Yuki Koike are listed for the men's 100m. Tada has a 10.01 personal best, while Koike has run 10.06. Both are part of Japan's Asian Games sprint team.The wider Asian field has also produced several sub-10.10-level performances this season, with Japan's Rikuto Higuchi at 10.01 and other Japanese sprinters around the 10.03-10.04 mark. Gurindervir's 10.09 and Kujur's 10.14 put the Indian pair firmly in that group.The 200m is an even tougher proposition on paper.Japan's Soshi Mizukubo has run 20.07 this season and won the Japanese national title. Thailand's Puripol Boonson has gone 20.03, a national record, while Kujur's Indian record remains 20.32.Kujur's own 2026 200m season has been less spectacular than his record-breaking 2025, but that has not altered how he sees the event.Earlier in the year, he qualified for the Asian Games with 20.74 at the National Inter-State Championships, a time comfortably inside the qualification mark but well outside his 20.32 national record.The clock is no longer driving Kujur's racesHe has since been thinking less about producing a particular time in every race.In 2024, Kujur said, he spent an entire season running around 20.5 and 20.6. Then came 20.40 at the Senior Federation Cup in 2025, followed by 20.32 at the Asian Championships.“So when it has to happen, it will happen,” he said. “No matter how much you push, the conditions should be like that, competition should be like that, and the atmosphere should be like that. And it's all about that day.”There is a similar change in his 100m target.The conversation around Kujur had once centred on whether he could break 10 seconds. Kujur has moved his own target further.“No, I don't think of 10 flat, now I think of running 9,” he said.Even after running 10.21, he felt there was more there.“Even today, when I stood in 10.16, I thought, this is not a 10.16 race,” he said. “So it's okay, when it has to come, it comes.”The lessons from his first international campaignWhat matters now is getting the body to the right point. Kujur's first major international experience came at the 2025 Asian Championships, where he won bronze in the 200m. He says he was under pressure because he was representing India officially for the first time.He does not expect that feeling to return in Japan.“And the mistakes I made in the Asian Championships, I won't make again,” he said. “Because I was first international. Officially, I was representing India. And I was under pressure for that.”Since then, he has raced at the World Championships, on the Continental Tour and at other international competitions. His coach has also encouraged him to use those races to experiment.“With the upcoming LA Olympics, [the coaches have told me] don't miss any chance to make a mistake. And our ultimate aim is the LA Olympics,” Kujur said.Learning when to push - and when to back offThe Asian Games therefore arrive after a season in which Kujur has learned more about managing the work around the races.That will be particularly relevant in Aichi-Nagoya. Kujur says the heat and humidity will not be new to him.“Yes, it is the same condition where I train. Same humidity, same heat,” he said. “And last time I competed in the World Championship. So I have an idea how to keep my body there and how to maintain things.”“I know what form I am in, how my body is behaving, what time to take my body, when to peak, when to reduce the load, all the things that we have learned from the last year, how to maintain everything,” he said.There is also a sizeable support system behind Kujur's preparation.“I have a lot of people on my support, like Reliance, Odisha Government, then TOPS, Athletic Federation of India, and others, and Puma, they never let me down,” he said. “Everyone wants me to improve, in every field, whether it's performance wise, or mental peace, or anything else. As a normal human being, everyone wants me to improve.”The expectation he carries into his first Asian Games is also different from the one he had at the Asian Championships.‘I know I am going to do well’He has already won an Asian medal. He now wants to win one at a bigger multi-sport event.“The success of the Asian Games will be a life-changing moment for me, because I have never won a medal in such a big game,” he said.Asked which of the 100m, 200m and relay he considered his best medal opportunity, he did not pick one.“Sure shot medal,” Kujur said. “I have won all three.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Serena Williams opens up about life-threatening pregnancy complications and the experience that changed her forever
articles.summary: International Sports News: Serena Williams knows what it means to fight through pain when the world is watching. But one of her toughest battles came away from the tennis court,.
articles.body: Serena Williams knows what it means to fight through pain when the world is watching. But one of her toughest battles came away from the tennis court, after the birth of her first daughter. Years later, the 23-time Grand Slam champion is still speaking openly about the experience. Her story has become more than a personal account. It has helped her understand how widely women can struggle to be heard when they need medical care.Serena Williams recalls the pregnancy complications that changed her outlookWilliams welcomed her daughter, Alexis Olympia, with husband Alexis Ohanian in 2017. The birth quickly became a medical emergency when she needed an emergency C-section.Her problems did not end after delivery. A coughing fit caused her wound to reopen, and doctors discovered a large hematoma in her abdomen. She then faced a pulmonary embolism, a serious condition involving a blood clot that blocks an artery in the lungs. The complications led to several surgeries and a six-day medical ordeal.For Williams, one of the most important parts of the experience was realizing how vital it was to speak up when something felt wrong.“I knew something was wrong with me and it was super important that I was heard,” Williams shared during the Forbes Power Women’s Summit 2026. “Thankfully, my doctor listened to me. The nurses did, but I was so fortunate enough to have a doctor that did and literally saved my life.”That experience stayed with her.Williams has since spoken about the difficulties women can face during pregnancy and after childbirth. At first, she believed her experience might have been linked mainly to her background. As she heard from other women, however, her perspective changed.“You know, when I told my story, I didn’t realize how many people could relate,” Williams shared during the summit. “And then at first I thought it was just a minority problem, but then I realized it’s a women’s problem.”Her observation points to something bigger than one difficult birth. Women from different backgrounds can face frightening experiences during maternity care, and Williams has used her platform to draw attention to those concerns.Serena Williams uses her experience to advocate for women's healthcareWilliams has not kept her story private. She has repeatedly used her public profile to push for better healthcare access, especially for women and communities that can face barriers to quality treatment.She also brought some humour to a serious conversation when discussing how different she believes healthcare might look if men experienced childbirth.“So many women from every single background had a nightmare’s tale of their birth, you know? And so— and then it boiled down to I thought, ‘Well, gosh, if men were giving birth, they would have sweets [and] like all kinds of medicines,’ ” she jokingly added. “So it wouldn’t be the same problem at all.”Her advocacy now extends into her work with the Reckitt Catalyst program, where she has served as the first entrepreneur-in-residence. The initiative supports entrepreneurs developing solutions in areas including health, hygiene, water and sanitation.For Williams, the work is personal. She understands that healthcare affects entire families, not just individual patients.“What these women are doing is they’re really letting us know that women’s healthcare is so important, and healthcare in general, because also we’re talking about women who take care of the kids, you know, I take care of my kids mostly,” she explained.Her own family has since grown. Williams and Ohanian welcomed their second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, in August 2023.The tennis icon has also shared practical ideas for improving maternal care. In a 2018 CNN opinion piece, she pointed to access to midwives, functioning health facilities, clean water, basic medicines, nutrition, breastfeeding and skin-to-skin contact as areas that can make a difference.Her message remains direct.“Together, we can make this change,” she said at the time. “Together, we can be the change.”For Serena Williams, the story of her first pregnancy is no longer only about what happened to her. It has become part of a much larger mission. By speaking about the moment she needed doctors to listen, she hopes more women will be heard before a crisis becomes life-threatening.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Trinity Rodman’s painful revelation about father Dennis Rodman resurfaces: ‘Extremely selfish human being’
articles.summary: International Sports News: Trinity Rodman’s comments about her father Dennis Rodman are back in the spotlight after an X account shared a clip from her 2024 Call Her Daddy inter.
articles.body: Trinity Rodman’s comments about her father Dennis Rodman are back in the spotlight after an X account shared a clip from her 2024 Call Her Daddy interview. The US soccer star spoke openly about their strained relationship and said Dennis was not a real father figure in her life. She also recalled a 2021 playoff game when he appeared without warning. Rodman said the visit affected her so much that she cried during the game. The old clip is now drawing fresh attention to what she said about her childhood and her relationship with him.Trinity Rodman says Dennis Rodman was absent from her lifeIn the December 18, 2024 episode of Call Her Daddy with Alex Cooper, Rodman gave her most detailed account of the relationship. She said she had tried to protect her father publicly for years, but felt she could no longer hide how much his absence had affected her.“He’s an extremely selfish human being… I think everything has always been about him,” Rodman said. She then made her view clear: “He’s not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else.”Rodman said she wanted a real father-daughter bond. She spoke about wanting a genuine hug from him and said hearing his voice could bring up feelings connected to missing him and the hurt she carried. She also said she sometimes answered his calls mainly so she could feel she had done the right thing, rather than because she wanted to rebuild the relationship.Rodman has also described financial hardship after her parents’ split, including periods when the family lived in a Ford Expedition and motels. She has credited her mother as the main source of support while she built her soccer career.Why Trinity Rodman still remembers the 2021 playoff gameRodman also talked about a moment from her rookie season in 2021, when Dennis unexpectedly appeared at a Washington Spirit playoff game. She said she had not spoken with him for months, and realizing he was there brought up emotions she could not control.“The whistle blew and I was so mad,” she recalled. “You took this happy moment from me. You f**ked with my head again.”Rodman said she later confronted him, telling him, “F**k you,” before crying in his arms “as if it’s a daddy-daughter [moment].” She questioned whether his appearance was really about supporting her or being seen at the game.Rodman hoped the meeting could lead to a closer relationship. Instead, she said they returned to having little contact.Dennis Rodman later responded publicly, saying he was sorry he had not been the father she wanted and insisting that he still tried to be there for her. Rodman rejected the response on Instagram Stories, calling it “A joke” and adding, “Wiping my hands with it. I’m done. Thank you.”The latest X post is recirculating an old interview, not revealing a new account from Rodman. The original comments came from her December 2024 conversation with Alex Cooper, where she spoke about a relationship that had remained painful and distant for years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: Satwik-Chirag pair returns to defend Hangzhou crown
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: The timing of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty’s resurgence could hardly be more telling. Just two weeks before they come to Japan to defend .
articles.body: The timing of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty’s resurgence could hardly be more telling. Just two weeks before they come to Japan to defend their Asian Games crown, the duo won the China Masters title — thereby giving a timely reminder that when it matters the most, India’s formidable men’s doubles pair is hitting top gear once again.Three years ago, Satwik-Chirag made history at the Hangzhou Asiad, winning India’s first-ever gold medal in badminton at the at the Asian Games — a feat that had eluded even legends such as Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu.Given the depth and quality of Asian badminton, the triumph carried a significance comparable to an Olympic or World Championships medal.This time, though, the equation is different. Satwik and Chirag arrive not as hungry challengers writing an origin story, but as defending champions with a target firmly on their backs. Yet, neither Satwik nor Chirag appear keen to carry that weight onto the court. Chirag has made it clear that the pair simply wants to enjoy themselves, as they always have, refusing to let expectation dictate their mindset.For coach, Kim Tan Her, the China Masters title is more than just a confidence boost. It is momentum with substance. Winning a title immediately before a major event, he believes, gives the pair a genuine edge and leaves them feeling considerably more assured.The road to a repeat, however, will be anything but straightforward.Aichi-Nagoya is likely to present a gauntlet of elite combinations: two pairs each from China and Indonesia, along with Korea’s world No. 1 duo. Indonesia’s Leo Rolly Carnando-Daniel Marthin and Fajar Alfian-Muhammad Rian Ardianto, as well as China’s world champions Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang, loom as among the sternest challenges to India’s title defence.What continues to set Satwik and Chirag apart is how far their game has evolved beyond brute force. The thunderous smashes remain, but opponents have become increasingly adept at blunting that weapon. So, the pair has learned to build points differently. Instead of rushing to unleash their “most-favoured weapon” — the smash — the pair is now using early exchanges to manipulate rallies, move opponents around and create openings.Chirag, once known primarily for his work at the net, has also sharpened his defence into a potent counter-attacking weapon, making the pair considerably harder to unsettle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
OL Lyon nes showed no mercy with challengers Paris FC in Week 2 of the Arkema Première Ligue (APL). Bagging both second wins, Paris Saint-Germain and Les Marseillaises keep up the pace for now.

Here's a breakdown of the action this weekend in France .

OL Lyonnes expected a challenge against Paris FC, and they got one, even though it lasted only for a half. At the Groupama Stadium, Paris arrived with intent and looked like they could pull off an upset against the French giants. But neither Manoly Baquerizo's header nor Mariam Toloba's strike, both good half-chances, found the back of the net.

For Sandrine Soubeyrand's side, that window of opportunity closed for good as the first half drew to a close. Headers from Marie-Antoinette Katoto , ending a nine-game goal drought, and Melchie Dumornay , in another link-up with Jule Brand , gave Lyon a comfortable lead at the break.

After the restart, the Fenottes again leaned on Katoto and Dumornay. Following a strong drive into the box from Salma Paralluelo , the French striker found the net for a second time with a backheel flick before being subbed off. But her exit was hardly a gift for the Parisians.

Introduced from the bench was the one and only Ada Hegerberg . The 2018 Ballon d'Or winner had an instant impact with a goal on her first touch following Dumornay's cross. Minutes later, the Haitian maestro's delivery was volleyed home by the 31-year-old Norwegian striker. Hegerberg then completed her hat-trick with a commanding header in stoppage time.

Like Katoto, Dumornay also finished with a brace thanks to one from the penalty spot, already reaching five goals this season. Paris FC's only consolation came through a fine piece of skill from Clara Mateo .

7-1 is becoming Lyon's trademark scoreline, after the exact same result saw them dump Fleury in last week's season opener . Paris FC must now be wondering whether they are genuine title contenders after this rout.

PSG still perfect, Karchaoui leads the way

PSG, the capital's other side, kept their fast start going with another solid 2-0 win, this time against Strasbourg , supposedly a tougher opponent than Lens last weekend. Led by Sakina Karchaoui, the home side settled matters early: the captain's beautifully bent free-kick found Merveille Kanjinga's header for the opener.

With more than 20 chances, PSG looked effortless but not lethal. Karchaoui's penalty, as the clock struck 60, sealed the game. Paulo César's side keeps pace with Lyon at the top of the league with two wins in two games.

Marseille edge past Lens to complete podium

Still searching for cruising altitude, Marseille ground out a patient win to finally get some reward (1-2). Visitors Lens answered Louise Fleury's opening goal with Léa Notel's powerful strike following Roseline Éloissant's great run down the right flank.

Despite a dominant showing with 60 percent of possession and 16 attempts, the Phocéennes only broke down the Sang et Or's resistance thanks to Carina Baltrip-Reyes on a set piece.

The Panamanian defender, who joined from Lazio this summer, rose above the pack to head in Lexi Missimo's late free-kick cross. Another narrow, one-goal win for Marseille, while a hopeful Lens side remain winless.

Calba helps Fleury find light against former club

Nantes and Fleury, both top half contenders, shared the points after a balanced match with both teams holding the ball an equal amount of time (1-1). The Canaries thought they had secured their first league win of the season thanks to Madeline Roth's first half header.

But Lucie Calba punished her former club with a stoppage time tap-in after Sanâa Mssoudy slalomed past Nantes' defence. Both sides are still looking for momentum this season.

In other news, Saint-Malo picked up a historic first win in the French top flight against Montpellier (1-0). A superbly curved early free-kick from Megan Rucker did the job for the Diablesses, who resisted the visiting side's domination.

In their first appearance in the city's 30,000-seater stadium, Toulouse hoped for a better outcome (1-2). Le Havre turned the game around after Julie Rabanne's early penalty, thanks to youngster Thaïs Gallais' first professional goal and an unlucky own goal from Mariam Diakité. The Violettes are still sitting at the bottom of the table.

Match-day 3 preview: Paris FC and Strasbourg looking to bounce back

The APL returns this weekend for matchday 3. Strasbourg and Paris FC will hope for a different outcome when they face off against each other. OL Lyonnes travel to Le Havre, as the hosts hope for anything but another beating, while Montpellier and Marseille clash in the South derby.

articles.title: Where Will the Top Padres Prospect Wind Up in 2027?
articles.summary: Ethan Salas has spent plenty of time in the San Diego Padres organization. After being signed out of Venezuela as a 16-year-old catcher, he quickly became th...
articles.body:
Ethan Salas has spent plenty of time in the San Diego Padres organization. After being signed out of Venezuela as a 16-year-old catcher, he quickly became the Friars' No. 1 prospect. He fell from grace a bit due to a back injury that kept him out for most of the 2025 campaign. Since then, however, he's gone on a tear. Between two levels of the Padres' minor leagues, Salas hit .296/.374/.448 with 156 total bases in 96 games. In that time, Salas notched 21 extra-base hits with 10 homers.

That production earned Salas a call to the big leagues . Part of that decision was due to the major-league rosters expanding on September 1. But the young catcher did everything to earn that role with the big-league club. He's yet to break out immediately, getting the occasional start and pinch-hit opportunity. But Salas finally got his first hit on Sunday evening versus the San Francisco Giants . In the fourth inning of the series finale, the backstop tripled off the right-field wall. He's the youngest player to triple for his first career hit since Manny Machado did so on August 9, 2012.

Where Will Padres No. 1 Prospect Ethan Salas Be in 2027?

Salas is certain to receive an invite to spring training. The 20-year-old catcher has been invited to each of the last four spring trainings. In that time, Salas hasn't played that well. The best slash line he's compiled was .222/.273/.333 (eight games) in 2024. The catcher has flashed plenty of potential, but never in Cactus League play. It's possible that something changes this season, forcing him onto the Opening Day roster, though it seems incredibly unlikely.

The Padres have two viable catcher options in Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin . Campusano has been much better at the plate this season. The backstop has had a breakout year at the dish with a .275/.374/.450 slash line. On the other hand, Fermin has struggled quite a bit with a .195 batting average. That said, Fermin's defense has proven quite valuable behind the plate. With that tandem, San Diego has options ahead of Salas. That makes it difficult for Salas to make it onto the major-league roster as a starter.

Because of that, Salas seems unlikely to be vying for a starter role in spring training. If he readily clears Fermin offensively, it's possible he gets selected for a bench role. That being said, it seems far more plausible that the Friars decide to leave Salas in the minors for some time. Despite those great numbers in the minors this season, Salas played just 24 games at the Triple-A level. That's not nearly enough time to develop against higher caliber pitching.

San Diego will likely want to bide their time with Salas. It's possible that he spends some time shuttling between Triple-A El Paso and the majors, but Salas seems all but certain to begin the 2027 season in Triple-A. He's spent some time with the big-league club, but hasn't proven success during that time. Even if he started raking for San Diego, it just doesn't seem like a viable option for the top prospect's future.

Without a clear path to the big-league roster and needing some time to develop at the plate, it is incredibly likely that the Friars send Salas to the El Paso Chihuahuas. In those 24 games with the team, Salas had a ridiculous .326/.410/.539 with eight extra-base hits and three homers. Those flashes of potential have been growing in Salas over his year in the Padres' organization. If he can build on that potential, he'll soon be the catcher of the future for San Diego.

However, it likely won't come until (at least) 2028. With Campusano not set to become a free agent until 2029, and Fermin following in 2030, Salas won't have a ready opportunity to start behind the dish until one of those two departs. If nothing else, Fermin's bat could regress enough that San Diego opts to give Salas a chance with the big-league club. That still seems to be a long way off for the top prospect, but hopes remain high within the organization for Salas' development.

articles.title: 'A lot of grit': Yankees clinch playoff berth after rallying past Twins
articles.summary: The New York Yankees secure October baseball while keeping pressure on the Tampa Bay Rays.
articles.body:
Monday's 8-3 comeback at the Minnesota Twins gave the Yankees the series-opening win, their sixth victory in their past seven games and a playoff spot entering the 2026 regular season's final two weeks.

"You start back in February and the goal is to go play in October and go win a championship," New York manager Aaron Boone told YES Network near the dugout at Target Field after the game, which brought the Yankees to 87-63. "And we've checked that first box and have that opportunity now, and obviously there's a lot of important games still in front of us here the rest of the way, but we're excited that we'll be able to take our shot. Feel like the group's coming together at the right time, but today's a good day."

The Tampa Bay Rays lead the American League East by 3.5 games, but the Yankees have a chance to take the division with next week's four-game series at Yankee Stadium.

They do so with Aaron Judge , who homered in his sixth game back from a three-month absence on the injured list, among those entering the mix as the Yankees ramp up against the Twins (70-80).

"It's one thing as a team we try to talk about every series ... as we get down the stretch -- just clean up the little mistakes, trying to fin-tune the situational hitting," Judge said . "So, I was just trying to do a job there. You've got guys on base, guys in scoring position. Either move 'em over or drive 'em in. So, I'm just happy to drive in add more runs there and let our pitchers do the thing."

What makes the 2026 Yankees different from New York's World Series contenders of the past decade?

"Got a lot of grit," Judge said. "Even going into tonight's game -- Twins put some good at-bats against us. They go up 2-1. The offense wasn't really going. But we found a way to fight back there."

Entering Tuesday's 7:40 p.m. start in Minnesota, continuing the three-game series with the Twins, the Yankees possess the AL Wild Card's first spot by a sizable margin over the Boston Red Sox (82-68) and Cleveland Guardians (76-75).

"It's what you've got to deal with as a major league club," Boone said. "We've certainly had our fair share (of adversity) this year, and I feel like the guys have persevered through that to this point. "There's a lot of grit in there with these guys, which I love. And we're used to playing in tight, difficult situations, and hopefully that's something that serves us well in the month of October."

articles.title: José Soriano Flirted With Making Blue Jays History With Dominant Outing
articles.summary: Throughout their history, the Toronto Blue Jays have only seen one pitcher wearing their uniform toss a no-hitter, and that was Dave Stieb during the 1990 ML...
articles.body:
Throughout their history, the Toronto Blue Jays have only seen one pitcher wearing their uniform toss a no-hitter, and that was Dave Stieb during the 1990 MLB season.

During Monday evening's contest against the Detroit Tigers , starter José Soriano flirted with becoming just the second Toronto pitcher to achieve the feat in 36 years, but ultimately fell just short.

Soriano took a no-hit bid against the Tigers into the seventh inning before it was eventually broken up by Gleyber Torres , who hit a single up the middle.

Still, Soriano delivered a gem of a performance for the Blue Jays , who entered Monday's contest at 75-75 and have given themselves a sporting chance at being able to defend their American League championship with a Wild Card playoff berth.

Toronto Blue Jays Starter José Soriano Took A No-Hit Bid Into The Seventh Inning

While he came close, José Soriano ultimately won't become the first Toronto Blue Jays starter to throw a no-hitter since 1990.

During the contest leading up to his no-hit bid being broken up by Gleyber Torres, Soriano struck out Riley Greene , Dillon Dingler , Hao-Yu Lee , and twice struck out Spencer Torkelson .

articles.title: Chargers’ Jim Harbaugh Admits Major Coaching Regret After Disappointing Cardinals Loss
articles.summary: Jim Harbaugh entered the 2026 season under pressure to finally end the Los Angeles Chargers‘ playoff drought. His team’s last outing was a wild-card exit aga...
articles.body:
Jim Harbaugh entered the 2026 season under pressure to finally end the Los Angeles Chargers ' playoff drought. His team's last outing was a wild-card exit against New England in January, and Sunday's opener against Arizona Cardinals was supposed to start a new chapter. Instead, the Chargers fell 26-14 at SoFi Stadium. A day later, Harbaugh pointed the blame somewhere few expected.

Jim Harbaugh admits Chargers preseason mistake cost them against Cardinals

Harbaugh met reporters on Monday and steered the conversation back to August. He said he now regrets how little live action his first-team players received before the regular season began.

"We made some preseason-type mistakes. Now I wish we played our starters more in the preseason, to give them game reps," Harbaugh told reporters.

The numbers supported his concern. Los Angeles managed only 268 total yards while Arizona piled up 393. The Cardinals held the ball for more than 37 minutes. The Chargers converted two of eight third downs and went scoreless on three fourth-down attempts.

Justin Herbert completed 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception, and he was sacked three times. Omarion Hampton scored on an 8-yard run early, then lost a fumble inside Arizona territory in the second quarter.

The fourth quarter sealed it. Simi Fehoko blocked a punt deep in Chargers land, and Brissett found Trey McBride for a 3-yard score two plays later. Andrew Wingard added an interception soon after. LaFleur walked off 1-0 in a building where nobody expected it.

Harbaugh's preseason comment wasn't the only Week 1 decision facing criticism.

Jim Harbaugh's late offensive line call now faces scrutiny

Days before kickoff, Harbaugh named Kayode Awosika his starting left guard, closing a competition that had stretched deep into camp.

That group then surrendered three sacks and could not hold a fourth-and-goal snap from the Arizona 3-yard line late in the first half, a series Harbaugh chose over a tying field goal. The line's struggles followed Herbert into his postgame remarks.

"It's on us to be able to execute the protection plan," Justin Herbert said .

The timing stings. Harbaugh spent the summer offering bold public praise for his quarterback, and hiring coordinator Mike McDaniel pushed expectations higher still. By Sunday night, supporters were instead searching for outside explanations for an offense that never clicked.

Los Angeles sits 0-1 after a home defeat few predicted. Arizona moves to 1-0 and hosts Seattle next. The Chargers stay at SoFi Stadium for Week 2, welcoming the Las Vegas Raiders on Sept. 20, with tight end Brock Bowers listed day to day.

articles.title: ‘Fleece!’ ‘This NEVER Happened in Miami’ — Dolphins Fans Ready To Relitigate Jaylen Waddle Trade As Broncos Star Goes Missing vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins fans spent months hearing that Jaylen Waddle could become the piece that pushes Denver’s offense over the top. But his first regular-season ga...
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins fans spent months hearing that Jaylen Waddle could become the piece that pushes Denver's offense over the top. But his first regular-season game gave those fans plenty of reason to start looking back at that trade.

Waddle finished with just one catch for two yards as Kansas City rolled to a 31-10 win Monday night. His quiet box score was made worse by a third-down drop, and suddenly, Miami fans had plenty to say about the March trade that sent the former No. 6 overall pick to Denver.

Dolphins Fans Reopen Jaylen Waddle Trade Debate

The sharpest reaction came after the third-down miscue. One fan sarcastically wrote , "This NEVER happened in Miami."

It was the kind of moment that needed almost no explanation for a fan base that watched Waddle closely for five seasons.

Denver acquired Waddle and the No. 111 pick from Miami in March for the No. 30, No. 94 and No. 130 selections, a price that reflected how strongly the Broncos believed he could elevate their offense.

Waddle arrived with "missing piece" expectations after Denver reached the AFC Championship Game last season. That made Monday's disappearing act especially easy material for Dolphins fans.

Another fan added , "It actually just made me flinch, that's how bad my PTSD is from his huge drops"

One X user wrote , "I like Waddle but man those drop issues were a real concern."

Another fan pointed to Waddle's production in Miami, writing, "And somehow he who shall not be named helped him become a 3x 1000 yd wr. Crazy work."

The three 1,000-yard seasons are accurate. Waddle topped the mark in each of his first three NFL seasons before finishing with 744 yards in 2024 and 910 yards and six touchdowns in 2025.

Broncos' Big Waddle Bet Starts With a Dud

Denver did not trade premium draft capital for a Week 1 box score, and one poor night does not settle whether Miami or Denver won the deal. It does, however, give Dolphins fans their first chance to revisit the offseason conversation.

Waddle entered 2026 after posting an 80.9 WR Impact score from PFN in 2025, ranking No. 22 among qualifying receivers. Denver believed pairing his explosiveness with Bo Nix and Courtland Sutton would give Sean Payton's offense another dimension.

Against Kansas City, almost none of that materialized.

The Broncos produced just 176 total yards, Nix threw for 131 yards, and Waddle's first regular-season reception in orange and blue went for a mere two yards.

Kansas City pulled away for a 31-10 win while Denver's new star receiver barely made an impact.

There are 16 games left to make the blockbuster trade look smarter. For one night, though, Dolphins fans who spent the offseason hearing what Waddle might become in Denver got to enjoy the easiest form of football analysis: reopening the trade receipt.

articles.title: Padres stretch winning streak to 8, Machado and Tatis homer in 8-7 win over Rockies
articles.summary: Manny Machado and Fernandez Tatis homered, helping the San Diego Padres beat the Colorado Rockies 8-7 Monday night to match their longest winning streak this...
articles.body:
DENVER (AP) — Manny Machado and Fernandez Tatis homered, helping the San Diego Padres beat the Colorado Rockies 8-7 Monday night to match their longest winning streak this season at eight games.

San Diego (82-68) clinched a fifth straight winning season for the first time in club history. The Padres began the night with a 2 1/2-game lead over Arizona for the NL's final wild card.

Colorado has lost eight games in a row for the first time since August 2025 is 5-21 since Aug. 16. The Rockies (55-95) must win at least eight of their last 12 games to avoid becoming the first team with four-consecutive 100-loss seasons since the New York Mets from 1962-65.

San Diego is 9-1 against the Rockies this season and has won 19 of its last 23 games against the Rockies.

San Diego, which was outhit 14-13, led 6-1 in the fifth inning only for the Rockies to close 6-5 in the sixth. Each team scored a run in both the seventh and eighth innings.

Mason Miller pitched a one-hit ninth for his 37th save in 39 chances. He is tied for the NL saves lead with the St. Louis Cardinals ' Riley O'Brien.

Machado hit his 28th homer of the season and 397th of his big league career in the first and TJ Rumfield had a tying RBI single in the bottom half. Jake Cronenworth hit a go-ahead single in a four-run second that included Freddy Fermin 's sacrifice fly and Tatis' two-run homer, a 449-foot drive.

San Diego got run-scoring singles by Jackson Merrill in the third inning and Ty France in the seventh. and Dustin Harris ' RBI double in the eighth. Merrill had his 14th three-hit game this year, tying his career best.

Casey Mize (6-9) allowed two runs and eight hits in five innings for just his second win since he was acquired from Detroit on Aug. 3. He had been 1-3 with a in seven starts.

Mize had no strikeouts for just the fourth time in 111 career big league starts.

Tomoyuki Sugano (12-10) gave up six runs and eight hits in five innings, dropping to 0-5 in his last six starts.

Padres' RHP Walker Buehler (8-6, 4.61 ERA) squares off against Rockies' LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.37 ERA) in game two of the series on Tuesday.

Patrick Mahomes had a rousing return from his ACL injury, leading the Kansas City Chiefs to a 21-point blowout of the Denver Broncos , 31-10, at Arrowhead Stadium on Monday.

Kenneth Walker III was also phenomenal in his debut for the Chiefs, tallying 23 carries for 173 yards and one touchdown.

"Fun fact: Tonight is the first time the Chiefs have rushed for 200+ yards at Arrowhead since 2016," posted StatMuse.

Kansas City Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane snagged an interception off rival Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix on his first coverage snap of the first drive of his first NFL game — all before leaving the field with a shoulder injury.

It was an undoubtedly rough scene for Delane, the No. 6 overall pick out of LSU, after he battled a shoulder injury throughout training camp and the preseason as he tried to get up to speed in a complicated Chiefs defense.

"Mansoor Delane is questionable to return with a shoulder injury. "After his pick, Delane lands on his right shoulder. He wasn't on the field for the Broncos' 2nd drive."

David J. Chao, a former NFL team doctor for nearly two decades, offered a diagnosis from afar as well as hope for Delane to potentially get back on the field against Denver.

"By video, right AC joint sprain," Chao wrote in a caption on a repost of Taylor's report. "To locker room but possible to return with injection."
