articles.title: Rams change course with Myles Garrett as Sean McVay looks for response to opening loss
articles.summary: WOODLAND HILLS, Calif.
articles.body:
WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — The Los Angeles Rams hoped Myles Garrett could manage his injury and remain an effective part of their defense. After watching him struggle with limitations in the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers , coach Sean McVay said Monday that the team recognized it needed to change course.

McVay said the decision to place Garrett on injured reserve came after a postgame conversation with the outside linebacker, whose limited availability had already affected his practice time before the opener. The Rams had believed he could contribute while working through the issue, but the game provided evidence that approach wasn't working.

"We thought it was something that we'd be able to manage that wasn't necessarily the case," McVay said. "It was right after the game in terms of listening to how he felt, how he was able to impact the game, and even what you guys saw with how limited we had to be with him."

McVay did not provide a firm recovery timetable or specify the injury during Monday's availability. He mentioned a potential return in four weeks but cautioned against establishing expectations before the team had more information.

"I think it'd be unfair to him without having the totality of all the information to put any sort of timeline on it," McVay said. "We know that he'll be available in four weeks potentially and we'll take that a day at a time."

The setback leaves the Rams preparing for their next game with uncertainty surrounding two of their most prominent defensive players. Aaron Donald , who did not travel for the opener, remains in the process of getting ready to play, and McVay said the team has not decided whether he will be available Monday night.

McVay emphasized that Garrett's injury would not dictate Donald's return. He also said Donald's absence from the opener had no bearing on the decision to play Garrett.

"They don't have anything to do with one another," McVay said. "It's more about Aaron and how he can contribute to the collective. What does that look like with how he's feeling to be able to resume 11-on-11 and being able to play and do the things that he's capable of?"

While Donald's timing remains uncertain, McVay expressed no hesitation about his expectations once the defensive lineman returns. Asked whether he expects Donald to perform at the same level as before his retirement, McVay responded: "I do. That's what my expectations are and my level of confidence in him."

In Garrett's absence, Josaiah Stewart will be among the players asked to take on more responsibility. McVay praised Stewart's development and ability to contribute against both the run and pass, expressing confidence in a group that handled much of the work throughout training camp.

"He'll be asked to step up, as will everybody in that group," McVay said. "I'm confident in those guys and excited."

The Rams also have several other injuries to manage during the week. McVay said safety Kam Curl was doing well after experiencing ankle soreness and returning to the opener. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is dealing with shoulder and thumb issues but is expected to be ready for the next game, while tight end Davis Allen also returned to action in the opener.

Inside linebacker Omar Speights suffered a hip pointer and has swelling, although McVay said he was feeling better than anticipated and making progress.

Beyond the injury updates, McVay identified the passing game as the primary area requiring improvement after the loss to San Francisco . The Rams struggled to sustain drives and convert in key situations, preventing the offense from establishing continuity.

"The lack of efficiency and effectiveness in the pass game prevented us from getting any continuity," McVay said. "The big area of focus improvement will be in regard to the pass game and some of the different things that we can do collectively. And like I told you, it always starts with me."

McVay saw more encouraging signs in the running game, citing the space created by the blocking and the ability to move the line of scrimmage. He also praised Blake Corum 's work in limited opportunities and Quentin Lake 's defensive performance, including an interception, his communication and his activity against the run.

Those positives did not change McVay's assessment that the opener fell short of the Rams' standards across all three phases. His focus now is on correcting those problems without allowing one loss to carry into the next opportunity.

"Let's not ignore the things that we can learn from, but we can't lose twice to that," McVay said. "We've got to be able to move forward."

articles.title: Yankees news: Watch Aaron Judge blast his first home run since returning from IL
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are thrilled to have Aaron Judge back. After missing three months with a right rib stress fracture, Judge was activated on Monday. The...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are thrilled to have Aaron Judge back. After missing three months with a right rib stress fracture, Judge was activated on Monday. The Yankees were playing the Minnesota Twins on the road.

In the top of the eigth inning, Judge was up at the plate. With New York leading 4-2, Judge smashed it off reliever A.J. Minter for a three-run homer.

It was the perfect exclamation point for an 8-3 win. The Yankees also clinched a playoff berth . In the end, Judge finished the game going 1-for-4 with three RBIs.

Judge had endured months of grueling rehab and uncertainty about what the season had in store for him. In May, he began experiencing discomfort in his right shoulder and upper rib area. At first, it was thought to be a bone bruise, but it turned out to be a stress fracture.

Nevertheless, the Bronx Bombers persevered without Judge in the lineup. Now for the ninth time in 10 seasons, they are back in October.

Meanwhile, the Yankees are leading in the American League Wild Card standings. They are 6.5 games ahead of the second-place Boston Red Sox .

According to Yanks Go Yard, the magic number for the Bronx Bombers to clinch is down to one. On Wednesday, the Yankees will conclude the three-game series against the Twins.

Then, they will head to Arizona to play three games against the Diamondbacks . Afterward, they will be back home for four games against the Tampa Bay Rays . However, painstackingly tiresome, Aaron Judge is back where he belongs.

articles.title: Mets news: Francisco Lindor reveals how much NY misses Pete Alonso
articles.summary: The New York Mets may have been playing winning baseball since the trade deadline despite being a selling ballclub, but that turnaround of theirs was too lit...
articles.body:
The New York Mets may have been playing winning baseball since the trade deadline despite being a selling ballclub, but that turnaround of theirs was too little too late. The 2026 campaign was long gone for the Mets since then, and their disastrous 2026 season has made it so that some of their decisions during the offseason , in retrospect, look all the more disastrous.

One of the Mets' heavily-criticized decisions during the offseason was their choice to let star first baseman Pete Alonso go in free agency to the Baltimore Orioles . Alonso has been the epitome of consistency since breaking through in the big leagues in 2019. Not only does he rarely miss games, he averaged 41.3 home runs during his time in New York (excluding the COVID-shortened 2020 season).

In 2026, Alonso continues to be one of the best sluggers in MLB. Entering play on Monday, with the Orioles visiting the Mets at Citi Field, Alonso has 35 home runs and 100 runs batted in to his name in 2026. Suffice to say, the Mets have been sorely missing his production. But for Francisco Lindor , he's also missing Alonso as a teammate and as a person, having shared a locker room with him for five seasons.

"As a person, I do miss him, for sure," Lindor said, via SNY Mets on X.

However, Lindor is not blaming the Mets' horrible 2026 season on Alonso's departure. He's choosing to take the glass half-full approach, saying that the front office had their reasons for making the moves they did this offseason — only for underperformance and injuries to rear their ugly heads.

"You can see the numbers, but at the end of the day, I thought the guys that we acquired were going to help us win games. We just haven't played, we haven't performed to our best. It's one of those that, you see him on the other side like, 'wow, those are great numbers. That's Pete Alonso ,'" Lindor said.

"But, at the same time, you look in our clubhouse and you say, the guys that we have are capable of helping us win ballgames. We haven't stayed healthy and we haven't put the season together."

The Mets currently have a 69-81 record, and they must be looking forward to redeeming themselves in 2027.

articles.title: Old Fort snaps Colonel Crawford's 11-win streak in five-set thriller
articles.summary: This was the type of matchup that showcases the strength of the Northern 10 now and makes a case for best volleyball conference in the state.
articles.body:
PHOTOS: Old Fort at Colonel Crawford volleyball

NORTH ROBINSON - There were several instances in Monday night's five-set thriller against Old Fort where Colonel Crawford coach Jaime Valentine wanted to call a timeout.

But instead, she opted to trust her girls on the court to treat adversity as a learning experience.

"Philosophy-wise, that's one thing I feel strongly about," Valentine said. "I have to allow them to work through when they're in panic mode and learn how to calm it down again. There were moments I could've called a timeout, and would have if I had more than two, but I had to let them work through some of those jitters and learn to work with each other on the court in those moments.

"Because in the end, they're who's going to be on the court — not me — they have to learn to work together and work through those moments ... for the most part, they figured it out."

It was a lesson at the "school of hard knocks" as the state-ranked Eagles — 13th in Division VI by the Ohio High School Volleyball Coaches Association — saw their 11-game win streak come to an end in a 3-2 (11-25, 25-23, 25-15, 23-25, 15-10) loss to the Stockaders in a Northern 10 cross-division clash.

"We knew coming into tonight that it was gonna be a tough match," Valentine said. "And honestly, I would love to play those kinds of matches every single night. It's so competitive and it allows the girls to learn how to work through some of those nervous moments ... we had some plays that were unlucky there in certain circumstances, but that's how it rolls."

It looked as if Colonel Crawford would be well on its way to adding another W to the streak after a dominating performance in the opening set holding an Old Fort team — ranked 11th in Division VII by the OHSVCA — to just 11 points.

But the Stockaders shrugged that off and won the next two sets in convincing fashion despite the Eagles making a late eight-point run in the second to pull within two. And Old Fort appeared to be primed to close out the match in the fourth taking a 23-15 lead before Colonel Crawford's Reese Redman took over serving and proceeded to spark a 10-0 run to close out and send it into the fifth.

"I think it should have been a four-set match, but I'm glad we pulled it out with the way it started," Old Fort coach Erin Rau said. "That's a good team, to not have your best night and still come out with a win (is big)."

It was big considering Alaina Parr opened the fifth set with three consecutive aces for the Eagles forcing Rau into a timeout not long after trailing 6-3. From that point on, it was all Old Fort as the visitors closed out on a 12-4 run to steal away the final set capped off with an ace.

"Two top 15 teams ... that's probably how it should look with scores and everything," Rau said. "I was glad after the first set that we snapped out of it because sometimes you don't know ... that can set the tone, and it didn't for us."

It was the Stockaders' third match to go five sets in the last 10 days, twice against league opponents as they currently sit third in the West behind Calvert and Mohawk; Colonel Crawford is tied for first in the East with Buckeye Central.

"I'm very happy that we came to the N10 ... most nights it's a tough game, I like that," Rau said. "You have to show up every night and that's goig to help us even more for tournaments."

articles.title: 'Will leave no stone unturned': Kevin Pietersen backs Brendon McCullum's claim of making England the best in the world
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen backed Brendon McCullum's vision to make England the best white-ball team in the world ahead of the 2027 World Cup.
articles.body:
Kevin Pietersen has backed McCullum's England revolution after joining as white-ball mentor until the 2027 ODI World Cup in Africa.

McCullum revealed he personally approached Pietersen for the role despite the latter's previous public criticism of England's preparations.

Pietersen has already energised the squad within 24 hours, with McCullum wanting him to challenge the entire team environment, not just batting.

Kevin Pietersen backs Brendon McCullum: England white-ball mentor vows to 'leave no stone unturned' for World Cup glory

Kevin Pietersen has thrown his full weight behind Brendon McCullum's vision after joining England's white-ball setup as a mentor, declaring the pursuit of World Cup glory as the team's only focus.

The appointment immediately raised questions, and for good reason, as Pietersen hadn't been shy about criticising England's setup in the recent past. In 2025, he questioned how the team had prepared for the ODI series against India ahead of the Champions Trophy after The Three Lions went down meekly.

However, McCullum confirmed at a press conference ahead of England's opening T20I against Sri Lanka that reaching out to Pietersen was his decision, and his alone. He explained what happened when he made the first call, describing Pietersen's initial reaction as one of pure disbelief.

"When I rang him the first time, I said, 'Would you be interested in coming to work with England?' He thought I was joking for a start," McCullum said.

"And then he sort of mentioned, I've been quite critical of you guys in the past. I said, I have no problem with that, mate. There are parts of it I agree with, and there are parts I won't agree with. And that's fine. That's what the beauty of Kev coming in.

"He's obviously got an incredible pedigree as a player. A lot of our guys grew up watching and idolising Kev when he was in his pomp as a player as well."

Whatever questions existed about how Pietersen would fit into the environment were answered quickly, if McCullum's early read is anything to go by. The Kiwi was clear that he doesn't want Pietersen confined to working only on batting, but he wants a broader contribution.

"He's brought a ton of energy to the setup within the last 24 hours already," McCullum said.

"I've mentioned to him that I don't want him to just try and be buried in one specific skill set either. I want him to look across the environment and setup, and challenge me privately on ways we can improve or things we can do differently. Our relationship is good."

Pietersen himself wasted no time in signalling his alignment with McCullum's approach.

Writing on X, he put the objective in simple words: "Baz is crystal clear. Our white ball team will leave NO STONE UNTURNED in its pursuit to being the best they can be. Message is loud and clear and I hope all England fans hear it and back the team in trying to win next years CWC! 🙏🏽"

Pietersen and McCullum: A relationship built on mutual respect, not compliance

McCullum was asked if there's any residual tension between the two. However, his emphatic response dispelled all doubts.

"It's full of respect. We play against each other, and we've enjoyed spending the time together over the last little while or two, he said.

"I'm super excited to have him. I know he's super excited to be here. The boys are buzzing, and I'm pleased that we can add such a strong resource to what's already a very, very strong coaching staff of mine."

Pietersen also brings practical experience in the mentor's role, having worked with Delhi Capitals in the IPL in a similar capacity, so this isn't entirely new territory for him.

The partnership is unconventional, and that's exactly why it could work

McCullum's Bazball philosophy has always been about backing the unconventional. Picking a coach who once criticised your methods to be your white-ball mentor is a bold move by any standard, and one that a more defensive coach would never make.

The fact that McCullum not only initiated the conversation but brushed aside Pietersen's criticisms says a great deal about his self-assurance and his willingness to bring challenge into his environment rather than surround himself with yes-people.

Pietersen's appointment could turn out to be the X-factor. He played in a different era but faced similar expectations: the burden of being England's match-winner, the scrutiny that comes with playing for one of cricket's most watched teams. That experience is difficult to replicate through coaching courses.

Whether the two personalities can sustain a productive working relationship all the way to a World Cup final is the real question, and both men know there will be bumpy moments. But the early signs, energy, alignment, and mutual respect suggest this pairing deserves more than scepticism.

articles.title: Rockies’ late rally thwarted by Padres in 8-7 heartbreaker
articles.summary: Rockies came back from a 6-1 deficit, but still drop 8th in a row
articles.body:
The Rockies battled, but couldn't score the run they needed or prevent San Diego 's late insurance runs as they fell 8-7 in a heartbreaker on Monday night at Coors Field.

Colorado trailed 6-1 after four innings, but made a game of it before San Diego's shutdown, slider-throwing closer Mason Miller posted two strikeouts to earn his 37th save of the season — the Rockies' only two strikeouts of the game.

"We have lost a lot of tight games this year," Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer said. "…The next step is to start winning the one-run games and that happens throughout the game. There's moments in the first inning, there's moments in the ninth inning, and every inning in between where we can improve. But we are right there. It's just a matter of time before we start winning those one-run games."

The loss was the eighth in a row for the Rockies, while the Padres won their eighth straight. The Rockies are now 1-9 against San Diego this season.

In the end, it turns out a team that consistently beats up on the Rockies facing a pitcher who gives up his fair share of homers is a bad combo. Manny Machado and Fernando Tatís Jr. each homered early off Tomoyuki Sugano (菅野 智之) to put the Rockies at a disadvantage from the jump.

Sugano gave up two homers for the fourth time in his last seven games as the Rockies once again found themselves down early and without enough offense to come back.

Machado hit a two-out solo homer in the first inning to put the Padres up immediately. In the second inning, Jackson Merrill led off with a single, Xander Bogaerts drew a one-out walk and Rockies killer Jake Cronenworth hit an RBI single to put the Padres up 2-1. Freddy Fermin followed with a sac fly, which set the table for Tatis' two-run bomb to increase San Diego's lead to 5-1. Just like that, it was four hits, one walk and five runs.

"Tomo was behind in counts and, therefore, got hit hard like hanging a two-strike breaking ball to Machado in the first," Schaeffer said. "I just thought he was behind in counts and didn't get to really see his good stuff with two strikes.

Sugano was hit hard again in the third when he gave up a double to Ty France and Merrill hit his second RBI double as San Diego went up 6-1. Sugano got a double play to get out of the inning and gave up lone singles in the fourth and fifth innings, but didn't allow further damage. He was pulled after five innings, giving up six runs on eight hits with two stikeouts and one walk.

Casey Mize gave up a two-out double to Hunter Goodman and an RBI single to TJ Rumfield in the first inning when the Rockies briefly tied the game, but then regained control. Rumfield extended his on-base streak to 19 games, which is second-best in Rockies history.

Despite allowing a runner in each of the five innings he pitched, Mize didn't allow any more runs for the next three innings. In the fifth, Connor Norby singled and Goodman drew a walk, once again providing runners for the hitting machine that is TJ Rumfield. Collecting his second run-scoring hit, the first baseman cut San Diego's lead to 6-2.

After five innings, Mize gave up eight hits and two walks, but only allowed two runs.

"I thought we played a very good game. I thought we battled all day. We had Mize on the ropes from the get-go, traffic every inning, solid at-bats up and down the lineup. We let 'em off the hook a few times like with a double play ball [Tovar hit into one in the second inning]," Schaeffer said. "It's easy when you get down 6-1 and you're on a seven-game losing streak to mail it in. But the guys in that room didn't do that and that's why we're going to be good here eventually."

When Kyle Hart entered the game for San Diego in the sixth and issued back-to-back one-out walks to Adael Amador and Ezequiel Tovar , the Rockies finally took advantage. Jake McCarthy came up clutch with his 10th triple of the season to plate in his 79th and 80th RBIs and cut San Diego's lead in half.

Norby followed with a sacrifice grounder to score McCarthy and the Rockies were back in the game only down 6-4. Goodman then hit a triple of his own, reaching base for the third consecutive time, but the Rockies rally was done. Unfortunately, when Goodman came back out to catch in the bottom of the frame, he was struggling with left thumb soreness and had to leave the game. The injury came from a head-first slide on his triple.

"He jammed his thumb going into third base. We'll re-evaluate tomorrow," Schaeffer said.

In the seventh, Cole Carrigg smashed a 96-mph Bradgley Rodriguez fastball 424 feet to right field to cut the Padres lead to 7-6. The blast was Carrigg's eighth of the year.

In the eighth, Tovar singled and Norby came up with a huge double that once again cut the Padres' lead to one at 8-7. But Brett Sullivan , who entered the game after Goodman left injured, and Rumfield each grounded out to strand Norby at second.

In the ninth, Kyle Karros posted an infield single that hit off Miller's leg, but Amador hit a high-bouncing chopper to end the game.

Blas Castaño relieved Sugano in the sixth and put up a scoreless 1.1 innings. Mark Manfredi's outing didn't go as well. With one out in the seventh, he walked Dustin Harris . Harris then stole second and advanced to third on a wild pitch before coming home to score on a France RBI single.

Juan Mejia was able to end the seventh without surrendering any more runs, but he did give up one in the eighth when he gave up two singles and then an RBI double to Harris. Jordan Romano threw a scoreless ninth to give the Rockies a chance.

The Rockies actually struck out the Padres eight times, while only striking out twice themselves (both off Miller in the ninth). Sugano, Castaño, Mejia and Romano all posted two strikeouts apiece.

The Rockies and Padres will be back at it on Tuesday at 6:40 p.m. Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.37 ERA) is back from the IL and will start for Colorado, while Walker Buehler (8-6, 4.61 ERA)will start for San Diego.

articles.title: Down, but also out
articles.summary: A Minor League lineup, and a 4-game losing streak.
articles.body:
On Sunday, in their broomstick loss to the San Diego Padres , the San Francisco Giants rolled out a lineup almost entirely devoid of players who had been on the roster when the year began. In the recap, I took note of the almost unfathomable turnover: two players from the Opening Day roster, one player from another team's Opening Day roster, two players who began the year in AAA Sacramento, two players who began the year on other AAA teams, and two players who began the year in AA Richmond.

As if to one-up themselves on Monday against the St. Louis Cardinals , the Giants turned it up a notch, removing Jung Hoo Lee from the lineup for a veteran off-day. The final tally:

One player from the Opening Day roster ( Christian Koss ) One player from another Opening Day roster ( Brett Harris ) Two players from AAA Sacramento ( Bryce Eldridge and Grant McCray ) Two players from other AAA rosters ( Shay Whitcomb and Andrew Knizner ) Three players from AA Richmond (Jonah Cox, Turner Hill, and Scott Bandura)

And for half the game, you, I, and everyone watching the game, were convinced that the Giants were going to get no-hit by Quinn Mathews .

Play stupid games, win stupid prizes. Play Minor League games, win Minor League prizes. Play 95-loss games, flirt with 100 losses, which is still in play if the Giants turn their current four-game losing streak into a 15-game skid. Just tack on 11 more losses, how much can it hurt?

Yes, the Giants didn't have a baserunner in the first inning, and they didn't have a baserunner in the second inning, and they didn't have a baserunner in the third inning, and Eldridge broke up the perfect game with a walk in the fourth inning, and they didn't have a baserunner in the fifth inning, and then, mercifully, McCray bopped a double to lead off the sixth, and New Rock Bottom watch was called off.

The small victories we uncover this time of year. They really are something, aren't they?

Stunningly, given the way that Mathews had carved through the Giants lineup, they even converted that first hit into a run, when Koss moved McCray to third on a productive groundout, and Cox brought him home with a single. With that, the deficit was cut in half, from 2-0 to 2-1, and the offense was off and running.

Off and running and stalling, unfortunately. McCray's hit opened the floodgates for the knocks, but Cox's RBI did not open the floodgates for the runs. Whitcomb and Hill hit back-to-back singles to open the seventh, but they would never score: Harris bunted them over, but a Lee pinch-hit fly ball fell short of being deep enough to score Whitcomb. After Knizner drew a walk to load the bases, Mathews was replaced by Justin Bruihl , and while McCray fought to the seventh pitch in a tough lefty-on-lefty matchup, he ultimately lost.

It wasn't their only rally that fell short. Eldridge smacked a two-out single in the eighth, and a pinch-hitting Drew Gilbert made like his first name and drew a walk, but Hill lined one sharply into an infielder's mitt. Lee smacked a one-out single in the ninth, and a pinch-hitting Drew Cavanaugh (another player who began the year in AA) followed it up with a walk, but McCray struck out and Koss grounded out and the game was over, as meek as it possibly could have been.

The Giants remained in it, however, thanks to the rarest of things (for them, that is): some good run suppression from the pitchers. It began with A Very Landen Roupp Start.

Ever since Roupp's brilliant first month of the season, you can fit nearly all of his starts into two very similar but very different categories:

Get into a lot of trouble, but somehow get out of it

Get into a lot of trouble, and very much don't get out of it

That's kind of it. He has bad games, and he has good games where he looks like he might have a bad game but then somehow doesn't. It's basically like watching Camilo Doval , except for five innings instead of one, and with a little side sprinkle of bigotry to make you less upset when it doesn't work.

Except in this game he introduced a third category of start:

Get into a lot of trouble, somehow get out of it, then get into more trouble and the bullpen can't get out of it

Roupp gave up a single to the very first batter he faced, but then immediately induced a double play. He walked the next batter, then got out of the inning.

He gave up a leadoff double in the second, followed by a two-out walk, but again got out of the inning.

In the third, it was back-to-back two-out singles that started an ultimately futile Cardinals rally.

After a clean fourth, Roupp got back into trouble in the fifth, ceding a one-out single, a stolen base, and a walk. With 88 pitches to his name, and the Giants being very careful with him these days, Roupp's night was over. He had bent without breaking time and time again, but his own fate was now out of his hands, and instead in Reiver Sanmartin 's.

Sanmartin gave up on RBI single on the very first pitch he threw, which was followed by a walk, another RBI single, and the slow march to the mound from Tony Vitello.

From there, the Giants bullpen was, shockingly, nearly perfect. Joel Kuhnel escaped the bases-loaded, one-out jam, and tossed in a perfect sixth for good measure. Trent Harris, who I think is no longer auditioning for a role in next year's bullpen and is instead auditioning for a high-leverage role in next year's bullpen, was a dominant force in a perfect seventh. Carson Seymour easily worked around a leadoff single in the eighth.

But the damage was done by the bottom of the fifth, and by a Minor League offense. You get what you pay for and, well … I'm guessing none of you are paying much for this.

articles.title: MLB Injury Report: Core muscle injury ends the season for hot-hitting Rafael Devers
articles.summary: Jorge Montanez breaks down all of the relevant injury news around the league over the last week.
articles.body:
In this week's Injury Report, Rafael Devers will undergo core muscle surgery, ending his season three home runs shy of 40 with two weeks to play. Kyle Bradish is also likely done for the season as he landed on the injured list with an abdominal injury. And the Cubs are eyeing a Friday return for Dansby Swanson . All that and more as we review all of the latest injury news.

⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026 ! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.

Devastating news that seemingly came out of nowhere on Sunday. A day after slugging his 37th homer, the Giants placed Devers on the 60-day injured list with a core muscle injury, ending his bid to become the first Giants player to hit 40 homers since Barry Bonds in 2004. The 29-year-old first baseman had been one of the hottest hitters in baseball this month, carrying fantasy teams in September with seven homers and a .342 batting average. It's even more incredible to find out he's apparently been playing through the injury for some time. The team saw it best to shut him down for the final two weeks, with plans for Devers to undergo core muscle surgery. He's expected to be recovered and ready for spring training. With Devers out, the Giants now make for one of the top teams to target for streaming pitchers the rest of the way.

The playoff picture comes into focus, with the White Sox and Guardians set to clash to begin the week.

Bradish's season came to an end a day after giving up five runs over three innings on Saturday against the Blue Jays. Toronto placed the 30-year-old right-hander on the 15-day injured list on Sunday with lower abdominal discomfort. The 30-year-old right-hander was a popular sleeper pick after finishing the 2025 season strong in his return from Tommy John surgery. Instead, he struggled in his first full campaign back, posting a 4.12 ERA, 1.46 WHIP, and a career-low 21.2% strikeout rate.

Valdez suffered a hamstring injury on Friday against the Cubs, departing in the sixth inning. He was placed on the 10-day injured list with a left hamstring strain. The 22-year-old outfielder had come out of the gates hot in his debut, hitting .309 with ten homers in the first half. His high strikeout rate led to a second-half skid as he hit just .184 with seven homers since the All-Star break. Valdez's placement on the injured list coincides with Ryan O'Hearn's activation, with O'Hearn now filling in for designated hitter duties.

Swanson will begin a brief minor league rehab assignment with Triple-A Iowa on Tuesday. Manager Craig Counsell told reporters that the team is planning to activate him from the 10-day injured list on Friday for the start of a weekend series against the Reds. The 32-year-old shortstop has been out of action since mid-August with a left oblique strain. Nico Hoerner has filled in at shortstop with rookie Pedro Ramírez getting playing time at second base. Ramírez will likely shift to a bench role when Swanson returns.

Yesavage tossed 30 pitches in a simulated game in his last mound session and was cleared to start a rehab assignment with Triple-A Buffalo. He'll make a start on Wednesday and is aiming to throw two or three innings. The 23-year-old right-hander is making his way back from left knee meniscus surgery that has sidelined him since early August. This late in the season, he may make it back for just an appearance or two for the Blue Jays in the regular season before he's available for a potential playoff run should the team make the postseason.

Another pitcher looking to get some major league work in before the end of the season, Early was scheduled to make a second start with Double-A Harrisburg on Sunday, but the game was rained out. He could instead make a start with Triple-A Rochester this week before he's potentially cleared to make his Nationals debut before the end of the season. The 24-year-old left-hander has been on the shelf with left elbow inflammation since late June when he was still with the Red Sox .

More reinforcements are on the way for the Yankees ' pitching staff. Weathers is recovering from a left forearm flexor strain and is scheduled to throw another bullpen session on Tuesday. The 26-year-old left-hander had initially hoped to make it back before the end of the regular season, but it seems unlikely he'd get ramped up in time to rejoin the rotation. Instead, he'd be an option for either the starting staff or the bullpen in the postseason. Meanwhile, Schmidt will be making his return from Tommy John surgery this week and will be used in a relief role through the rest of the season and into the playoffs.

articles.body:
Jaylen Waddle had a brutal performance in his season debut throughout the Denver Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday night.

Waddle started the sixth season of his NFL career, his first with the Broncos . He spent the last five years with the Miami Dolphins before they traded him to Denver this past offseason.

Waddle looked to make a big impact in the receiving corps, joining Evan Engram , Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant in the attack. However, his objective proved to be tougher than he hoped for.

Waddle struggled against the Chiefs' secondary, only getting three targets from quarterback Bo Nix . Of those chances, he only caught one pass for two yards for the entire game.

How Jaylen Waddle , Broncos played against Chiefs

Jaylen Waddle and the Broncos have some self-reflecting to do. Their 31-10 blowout loss to the Chiefs is a big step back from the incredible progress they made last year.

The game started out as close with Kansas City leading 14-7 at halftime. His second half saw the best moments of the Chiefs, torching Denver 17-3 in the last 30 minutes of regulation.

Nix was unable to make big dents in the Chiefs' defense. He only completed 17 out of 28 passes for 131 yards and a touchdown and an interception, taking four sacks from Kansas City defenders throughout the game.

JK Dobbins led the run game with eight rushes for 36 yards as the team only totaled up to 61 yards on the ground. Evan Engram led the receiving attack with four catches for 43 yards and a touchdown, Pat Bryant had four receptions for 42 yards, while RJ Harvey caught four passes for 23 yards.

articles.title: Leigh Leopards and Wakefield Trinity ready for rematch as both clubs look to make more history
articles.summary: Leigh Leopards and Wakefield Trinity will do play-off battle once again for a spot in the semi-finals; Watch Wakefield Trinity vs Leigh Leopards in the Super League Eliminators, live on Sky Sports on Friday September 18, with kick-off at 8pm
articles.body:
Wakefield made history with a fourth-place finish in Super League, the highest in the club's history. Next on the list is reaching the semi-finals for the first time ever.

Leigh, meanwhile, have been making waves since their return to the top flight in 2023, winning the Challenge Cup and making the Super League semi-finals regularly.

The next step for them is making it all the way to the big dance.

For Joe Ofahengaue, to do that, the Leopards need to execute their game plan well. If they do that, they might just achieve the very thing that would mean "everything".

"It was a weird one. I thought the game shaped out to be all in Wakefield's favour," Ofahengaue told Sky Sports .

"That is not directing anything at the way the game was reffed. I just think we got our game plan wrong.

"They executed on a few mishaps in our defence but the Gods of rugby league have looked after us and given us a second shot.

"I think if we get our game plan on, we can really make some noise in this play-offs.

"Making it to the Grand Final would mean everything. I am banking on it.

"I am very emotionally attached to this squad. We have some key members of this squad leaving after this year and I want to send them out on a high note.

"The only way we can send them out on a high is if we win it.

"I don't want to look too for ahead or picture myself too far ahead but it is definitely a great goal of ours to reach Old Trafford."

Powell: We want to be genuine contenders

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell has been integral to the club hitting new heights, getting better and better every season.

They were only promoted back to Super League in 2025, finishing sixth, and now moving up to fourth, is a symbol that they are growing into a club that consistently challenges at the top.

The next symbol for them is making it wins against Leigh two weeks in a row.

"I would expect Leigh to step up intensity-wise," Powell told Sky Sports .

"I think they will go to another level. I mentioned that to the boys, I don't think you can expect that game to dictate anything that happens this week.

"We have just got to reset ourselves, go again, and we feel like we can play better actually.

"We are talking about progression each year. We finished sixth and we didn't feel like we did ourselves justice in the play-off game against Leigh in 2025.

"It's ironic that we face them again this year and a chance for a little bit of redemption. Being a genuine top four team is about getting to those semi-finals and giving yourself a chance to get to the Grand Final.

"It would be an awesome thing for the club. If we can do that, we will be pretty excited."

articles.title: Luke Littler says he needs 'crucial days off' as he continues chase for history ahead of World Series of Darts Finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler has admitted he needs to manage his schedule as he eyes a clean sweep of all of darts' major tournaments; watch the World Grand Prix from September 28 to October 4, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Littler has only played two Players Championship floor events, entered just three European Tour tournaments and skipped the recent World Series competitions in New Zealand and Australia.

The 19-year-old has taken a step back this year, limiting the number of lower-key events he has entered as he manages his schedule.

PDC president Barry Hearn recently fired a warning to the sport's top stars about regularly missing tournaments, but Littler says he can be his own master given his position at the top of the rankings.

"I think obviously it's just what's best for me and my family, just having those crucial days off. I think we're going to see more days off just to rest," he told the Press Association .

"That's all I'm doing. I'm obviously world number one, and there's a massive gap between myself and world number two. I can sort of take that step back and not go chasing every single tournament. It allows me to have, obviously, days off and weeks off, and yeah, just about balancing the schedule."

Littler is only taking part in the Players Championships this year in a bid to win a clean sweep of major titles.

However, having won the first six major titles of the year, he is aiming for all 10 and that requires him to qualify for the Players Championship Finals in November.

He is playing catch-up after skipping the first 26 floor events of the year, before beginning his bid in Leicester a fortnight ago.

Whether he continues his pursuit will depend on how he fares in the World Series of Darts Finals this week.

If he does not win the tournament in Amsterdam and can no longer secure every major title this year, he is unlikely to try and qualify for the Players Championship in Minehead.

"That's all you can do. I can't be looking forward any more than what's next, which is the World Series in Amsterdam," he added, speaking through his role with KP Nuts, which launched 'Hit the Bullseye', giving fans the chance to win £20,000.

"If I hopefully do win the World Series, then Tuesday and Wednesday I'll be in Den Bosch for the Pro Tours, try and qualify for Minehead. We've just got to see what happens in Amsterdam this weekend."

articles.title: Nairobi to host World Athletics Championships in 2029
articles.summary: Nairobi beats London, Munich and Rome to become the first African hosts, World Athletics says.
articles.body:
Nairobi will host the World Athletics Championships in 2029, beating off competition from London, Munich and Rome to become the first African hosts, World Athletics has announced.

The 2031 championships will be held in Munich, Germany, track and field’s governing body said after a council meeting on Tuesday in Budapest, Hungary, which hosted the recently concluded Ultimate Championships.

“We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council,” World Athletics president Sebastian Coe told a news conference.

The 2027 event has already been awarded to Beijing.

“This council decision today means we’re able to deliver our World Athletics Championships in Asia, Africa, and Europe over its next three editions,” the Briton added.

“Taking our championships to Africa for the first time will be historic. Nairobi has presented a compelling and emotional bid.”

Coe added: “It was important that the World Championships should come to Africa when we had the right host, the right bid, and the right circumstances.

“Nairobi has demonstrated emphatically that this is their moment to supercharge the development of our sport in Kenya and across Africa, leaving a compelling legacy that inspires a continent.”

Kenya, which failed with a bid for the 2025 World Championships, has previously hosted the 2007 World Cross Country Championships in Mombasa, the World Under-18 Championships in Nairobi in 2017, and the World Under-20 Championships in the capital in 2021.

Nairobi also staged the 2010 African Athletics Championships.

“Having also been part of the bidding process for 2025, the [Nairobi] team understood and grasped what was required and came back with a stronger proposition and a renovated Kasarani Stadium, which is currently undergoing a complete overhaul ahead of hosting the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) 2027,” said Coe.

articles.title: WWE's Best Monday of 2026, Penta's Star-Making Moment, Reigns Moves on Quickly, More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The September 14 edition of Raw on Netflix aired from Arena CDMX in Mexico City, Mexico, delivering big title action and Money in the Bank qualifiers.
articles.body:
The September 14 edition of Raw on Netflix aired from Arena CDMX in Mexico City, Mexico, delivering big title action and Money in the Bank qualifiers.

Roman Reigns overcame the best efforts of Penta to retain the World Heavyweight Championship. Chad Gable also retain his Intercontinental Championship against a game Dragon Lee.

Lola Vice debuted with a women's MITB qualifying win over Raquel Rodriguez and Kelani Jordan. Je'Von Evans defeated Big Cass and Austin Theory to earn a spot in the men's MITB ladder mach.

Check out all the fallout from a memorable night in Mexico City

Penta Aces Biggest Test Against Roman Reigns

The main event of Raw was always going to end one way: a Roman Reigns retention.

However, it served as a major test for Penta, who had a chance to deliver a classic that fans would not soon forget.

He did just that. This was one of the best matches of the year, driven by the athleticism and hard-hitting style of the challenger.

This match was a major win for Penta in terms of selling him as the kind of talent that can work with anyone in WWE and deliver a spectacle.

Not everyone gets chances like this, and fewer still get the chance to sell themselves to WWE as a must-book talent.

Penta did just that and should now be even more frequently highlighted on Raw going forward.

As Raw went off the air, WWE did not hesitate to announce the next match for Roman Reigns, confirming he would defend the World Heavyweight Championship against LA Knight at Money in the Bank.

The Million Dollar Megastar even laid out The OTC afterward to declare his intention to finally become a world champion.

This rushed post-show segment could have waited until next week, allowing fans to purely focus on Penta and his great performance.

By moving on so quickly, it diminishes the threat Penta posed. It was also unnecessary as Adam Pearce had already confirmed multiple times that Knight was the next man up for Reigns in past weeks.

Reigns vs. Knight already has a solid build behind it and should intensify into October unless The OTC does not appear for several weeks in the build-up.

Next week's biggest angle should be focused on truly solidifying The Million Dollar Megastar as a major threat to Reigns, trying to sell his chance of genuinely dethroning the champion.

Especially with the frequent surprise world title changes in recent months with every title but Reigns', this is a story WWE can sell with the right build.

Stephanie Vaquer's World Championship Victory was a Perfect Surprise

Over the weekend, Stephanie Vaquer became the new Women's world champion by defeating Liv Morgan at a live event in Santiago, Chile.

Even though La Primera is Chilean born and raised, it was still a genuine shock that she would win this big at a live event.

It was the first time that a women's world title had ever changed hands at a house show and the only time any WWE title had changed hands in South America.

While WWE could have given Vaquer the win on Raw, this historic moment solidified La Primera as a game-changing talent in WWE.

She earned this win through her hard work getting herself over in a short time with WWE and can carry the company forward as a fighting champion.

It was a surprise that Liv lost the world title at this stage of her career, but she remains a main event player going forward.

WWE also has an easy money match on the horizon when Becky Lynch and Vaquer step in the ring together for the first time.

Time to Start Pushing El Grande Americano on Raw

One of the biggest concerns with modern booking of AAA by WWE has been the complete separation of stories from one brand to another.

Dominik Mysterio and El Grande Americano got over big in Mexico, but they were both treated as midcard heels on Raw while main eventing AAA shows.

This separation of stories felt less concrete on Raw in Mexico City because WWE dealt with the immediate fallout of Americano taking the AAA Mega Championship from Dirty Dom.

The opening of the show sold Americano as AAA's top babyface, and this should continue when WWE return to the United States.

The awkward finish to the opening match to get heat back on The Judgment Day would seem to indicate that Americano will appear more on Raw soon.

However, nothing is certain, and this finish could have been a way to simply push the heels WWE cares more about.

Lola Vice and Kelani Jordan Immediately Show They Belong

In an exciting triple threat, Raquel Rodriguez, Lola Vice and Kelani Jordan battled for a spot in the Money in the Bank ladder match.

While Lola winning in her WWE debut was not completely surprising, it was a good indication that the company will push her strong, especially after pinning the Women's Intercontinental champion.

Even in a contest that could have used more time, The Standout also found her opportunities to show off.

As the current NXT women's champion, Lani is likely to remain in NXT for the short term, but she should be on a fast track to Raw when she loses the gold.

If WWE wants to heavily push The Standout, she could compete on Raw as champion, even defending the gold while she completes her NXT run.

This Raw women's roster needs both of these women to become immediate factors and massively improve the variety of competition.

Special attraction shows are often WWE's best, and this Raw in Mexico City was no different.

A hot invested crowd watched wall-to-wall action that sold how good this Raw roster can be.

Penta and Dragon Lee stood out for what they can do in the ring that no one else can match.

Both Money in the Bank qualifiers showed the value of strong matches with stakes on TV that show off underused talent like Je'Von Evans as well as new blood like Lola Vice and Kelani Jordan.

This was a show that highlighted exactly what WWE needs to do to make Raw must-watch TV every week.

While WWE may be known for long-winded promos and massive cinematic moments, the heart of a wrestling show is the wrestling.

Fans pay tickets to see the matches and enjoy the spectacle. Promos are valuable but can bog down a show quickly, especially in a modern WWE loaded with advertisements.

If WWE wants fans consistently invested, a blend of big matches and story development must be the focus rather than sacrificing in-ring time to ads and overlong talking spots.

articles.title: Trade Ideas for Connor Hellebuyck to NHL Contenders
articles.summary: From the moment the Winnipeg Jets 2025-26 season came to a disappointing end, going from the Presidents' Trophy to completely out of the playoffs, it was obvious that starting goalie Connor Hellebuyck was not happy with his current situation.
articles.body:
From the moment the Winnipeg Jets 2025-26 season came to a disappointing end, going from the Presidents' Trophy to completely out of the playoffs, it was obvious that starting goalie Connor Hellebuyck was not happy with his current situation.

He voiced his frustration with the way the season went, while also casting doubt as to whether or not the franchise had the right people in place to build a serious Stanley Cup contender. Given that he is now into his mid-30s and getting closer to the end of his career, he has to know the clock is ticking when it comes to getting him a Stanley Cup ring.

After speculation about his future started to build, things finally reached a boiling point earlier this month when he hade his trade request official.

Now that training camps are set to begin, Winnipeg has to deal with the possibility that Hellebuyck may not show up in an effort to further force the team's hands.

A trade seems inevitable, and there are a handful of teams around the NHL that could not only use a top-tier goalie, but should also have some interest in him.

But it is not going to be a simple trade, and it may not result in the type of return Winnipeg fans (or the organization) might be hoping for.

Why trading Connor Hellebuyck will not be easy

This isn't as simple as just trading a star player and getting equal or comparable value back in return.

Hellebuyck is the most decorated American-born goalie ever, and one of the best goalies of his era. His list of accomplishments is significant, including three Vezina Trophies and an Olympic Gold Medal. He has consistently shown he can lift mediocre teams to a higher level they probably have no business reaching.

On the surface, every team in the league should want that.

But when you trade for a player, and try to piece together appropriate value, you are not trading for what that player did in the past, or what they did most recently. You are trading for what they will do in the future, their age, their injury history, their positional value, their contract and everything else that comes with the player.

In Hellebuyck's case, you are talking about a 33-year-old goalie that is still owed $8.7 million against the cap per year for another five full seasons.

Do you trust him to still be that same goalie when he is 35 or 36? Or even this season? It is worth noting that, even with his Gold Medal winning performance at the Olympics, the 2025-26 regular season was the worst single season of his career. He posted a sub-.900 save percentage, was minus-0.4 goals saved above average (down from plus-41.6 the year before) and just 5.5 goals saved above expected (down from 39.6 the year before).

Maybe some of that was the result of the environment around him. Maybe it was a fluke year. Maybe he's already played his best hockey.

There is also the reality that Hellebuyck holds a lot of the cards here and, even with the trade request, can dictate where he goes. He might be flexible with Winnipeg on that, but he can still veto anything he does not like.

Goalie trade values are also a little tough to measure given the volatility of the position and how few truly elite players at the position get traded.

Just think about some of the more recent trades involving prominent goalies and what those returns looked like.

Jacob Markstrom has been traded twice over the past few years. This offseason he went from New Jersey to Florida as a 36-year-old goalie with two years and $6 million per year remaining on his contract. He brought back Evan Rodrigues, Jesper Boqvist and Ben Steeves.

That came two years after he went from Calgary to Florida as a 34-year-old goalie, also with two years and $6 million per year remaining at the time of that trade. He went for defenseman Kevin Bahl and a first-round pick.

After the 2023-24 season the Boston Bruins traded Linus Ullmark, one year removed from a Vezina Trophy and coming off a dominant three-year run, for backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo, forward Mark Kastelic and a first-round pick. Ullmark was 31 at the time and had two years remaining at $5 million per year remaining. It was mostly a salary dump trade for the Bruins.

Prior to the 2024-25 season a 27-year-old Logan Thompson went from Vegas to Washington for two draft picks (second-and third-rounders).

Young, and completely unproven goalies like Yaroslav Askarov and Sebastian Cossa have gone for returns centered around first-round picks

Hellebuyck is better than all of these guys, but he's also older than most of them, more expensive and requires a bigger (and riskier) financial investment.

All of that could be contributing to the reports that Winnipeg is not getting strong trade offers at the moment , while also wanting to focus on immediate help (including a goalie) to compete this season instead of futures.

So let's get into what some offers could look like, or what Winnipeg could be looking for in return.

The suggestion: Connor Hellebuyck to the Carolina Hurricanes for defenseman Alexander Nikishin (RFA), goalie Pyotr Kochetkov and a first-round pick

Could it use him? Absolutely. Would he be a likely upgrade over Kochetkov and Brandon Bussi? Almost certainly.

But Carolina has proven on a pretty consistent basis that it does not need an elite goalie to contend for a Stanley Cup, or to even win it. It's done pretty well for itself by piecing together a cheap goalie tandem and keeping enough salary cap flexibility to build out the roster around it.

Even so, the potential to land a proven, star-level goalie would be a great addition that would make the defending Stanley Cup champions even better and give them a great chance at making a repeat run.

The problem with Carolina as a destination, and with this idea? While the Hurricanes have three first-round picks over the next two years (and four over the next three years), and a young, NHL defenseman in Nikishin that still has some upside, it doesn't really have any young, NHL-ready forward help that would help fill Winnipeg's biggest needs on the roster.

The Hurricanes would have the salary cap space to take on Hellebuyck's deal, especially if Nikishin were the centerpiece and removing their need to re-sign him to his desired price tag. You also have to imagine that Hellebuyck would be receptive to playing for a team that has already shown it can win a championship.

Carolina reportedly approached Winnipeg with an offer similar to this earlier in the offseason and was turned away. Perhaps something like that could be revisited now that we know for a fact that Hellebuyck wants out.

The suggestion: Connor Hellebuyck to Vegas for goalie Adin Hill, 2028 first-round pick, and forward Braeden Bowman

You have to figure Vegas is going to make itself a part of this discussion. Not only because goaltending was a major issue for much of the 2025-26 season, but also because the Golden Knights just love making blockbuster trades and swinging for the fences when a big-name player becomes available.

But like Carolina, it's just not necessarily a great match in terms of potential assets.

The Golden Knights do have a goalie to offer back in Hill, and it would help ease some of the salary cap burden to shed his $6 million salary cap hit in the coming years. While Hill is not Hellebuyck and does not possess his track record, and even though he is coming off a down year, he has been a league average, to even slightly above league average goalie for most of his Vegas tenure. You can compete with him, especially as part of a platoon.

Vegas has accumulated a couple of future first-round picks that are probably move valuable to it as trade chips, while Bowman is a 23-year-old forward coming off a solid rookie season. He just signed a long-term contract and probably projects as a bottom-six forward, but could still play his way into a second-line role.

It's not great, but it's probably the best that Vegas (and Winnipeg) could do between the two teams. Especially given all of the trade protections that Vegas' NHL forwards have and their potential ability to block a trade to Winnipeg. And even then that could be complicated with Hill who has limited trade protections in contract.

Bowman is one of the few prominent, and tradable, players on the roster that has no such protections.

The suggestion: Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils for forward Dawson Mercer, goalie Jake Allen and a 2027 first-round pick

The Devils have had a really strong offseason and added a ton of forward depth to their roster.

It also might be a little too much forward depth, and something might have to give.

Along with that, goaltending is the one big obvious weakness the roster still has, especially after moving Jacob Markstrom to Florida.

Hellebuyck could help take the Devils from fringe playoff team to serious playoff contender and fill a big need.

They have plenty of first-round draft pick capital, and some forward depth to deal from, including the 24-year-old Mercer whose name has surfaced in trade speculation before.

He's not a star, but he's a 20-goal scorer that can play a variety of different roles and that has proven to be incredibly durable, having appeared in all 82 games in every season of his career. He makes $4 million this season, is a restricted free agent after this season and would then be eligible for unrestricted free agency without a new deal following the 2027-28 season.

The suggestion: Connor Hellebuyck to the Buffalo Sabres for goalie Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and forward Jack Quinn

Buffalo seems like the most obvious destination, and there were reportedly talks around the draft that centered around the No. 4 and 8 overall picks. Obviously, nothing came together at that point.

Goaltending was actually a surprisingly strong development for the Sabres in 2025-26, and it played a big role in the Sabres turning their season around and ending their 14-year playoff drought. The question is whether or not their goalies can repeat it and play at that level again. They might want somebody that is a little more proven and a little more consistent.

Luukkonen is really hit-and-miss on a year-to-year basis, alternating strong years and bad years. He can be a very good NHL goalie, but you never really know which version of him is going to show up. Winnipeg might be able to make him work as part of a platoon with Skinner, while moving his contract would help open up salary cap space for a Hellebuyck addition.

Quinn would be the young forward help Winnipeg would be looking to add, and he might be the best and most attainable NHL-caliber player that any of these teams might be able to offer. Buffalo might also have the forward depth to make him expendable.

He's 24 years old, has improved his offense every year he has been in the NHL and is coming off a 20-goal, 51-point season.

He has one year remaining on his current contract before becoming a restricted free agent.
